# Can ChatGPT edit videos? What it can and cannot do with video
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/can-chatgpt-edit-videos/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-23

ChatGPT cannot open a video file and cut, trim or colour-grade it the way an editor such as DaVinci Resolve or CapCut does. What it can do is plan and script videos, write captions and titles, edit photos, write code that assembles simple clips, and, through OpenAI's separate video model Sora, generate short video from text or images. This page sorts what works from what does not for making, editing and analysing video, how Claude compares, and which free tools sit alongside ChatGPT. Can ChatGPT edit videos? No, not directly. ChatGPT is not a video editor: it cannot trim your footage on a timeline, add transitions or export a finished edit of the clip you upload. It helps with everything around the edit. Give it your script or transcript and it will suggest where to cut, write an edit decision list with timestamps, draft on-screen text and captions, and propose B-roll ideas. It can also write commands for tools that do edit, for example an ffmpeg command that trims a clip from 00:01:10 to 00:02:30 or burns subtitles into a video, which you then run on your own machine. For real editing, pair it with an editor: DaVinci Resolve, Premiere Pro or CapCut, several of which have their own AI features such as automatic captions and silence removal. Can ChatGPT make videos? ChatGPT on its own produces text and images, not finished videos. Video generation comes from Sora, OpenAI's video model, which is offered alongside ChatGPT on eligible plans and in supported countries. Inside ChatGPT you can still produce the parts of a video: a script, a shot list, voice-over text, thumbnails and images for each scene. With its code tool it can sometimes assemble a very simple clip, such as a slideshow, by writing and running Python, but that is a workaround, not a video feature. For a talking explainer, the dependable workflow is ChatGPT for the script, a screen or camera recording by you, and an editor for the cut. Generated footage is best for short illustrative shots, not for a full lecture or product demo. Does ChatGPT generate videos? Not by itself. OpenAI's text-to-video model Sora generates short videos from a prompt or an image, and it is available through its own app and website for eligible users. Sora produces short clips with sound from a description such as "a time-lapse of a college campus at dawn". Results are impressive for mood and motion but can still get hands, text on screen and physics wrong, so plan to generate several takes and pick the best. Availability, clip length and limits depend on plan and region and have changed since launch, so check OpenAI's Sora page for the current details. Label AI-generated footage clearly when you publish it; platforms increasingly require this. Can ChatGPT make videos from photos? Not as a built-in feature, but it can write the command that does it. A slideshow from photos is one ffmpeg command, and image-to-video models such as Sora can animate a still photo. For a simple slideshow, name your photos in order and run: ffmpeg -framerate 1/3 -i img%03d.jpg -c:v libx264 -r 30 -pix_fmt yuv420p slideshow.mp4 That shows each image for three seconds and writes an MP4 that plays everywhere. Ask ChatGPT to add a fade between images or a music track and it will extend the command. If you want the photo itself to move, a camera push or a person turning their head, that is image-to-video generation, which needs a video model such as Sora rather than the chat. Can ChatGPT edit photos? Yes. ChatGPT can generate images and edit an uploaded photo from a text instruction: change the background, alter the style, remove an object, or combine elements from several images. Upload the photo and describe the change precisely, for example "replace the background with a plain light grey studio backdrop, keep the person unchanged". Edits regenerate the image, so faces and small text can shift slightly; check details before using the result in anything official. For pixel-exact work, such as a passport-style photo or brand assets, use a real editor like Photoshop, GIMP or Canva. Never use AI edits to misrepresent a real person or a document, and keep the original file. Can ChatGPT analyse videos? Only in limited ways. The dependable method is to give ChatGPT a transcript and a few key frames as images. It reads those well, while full-length video understanding is stronger in models built for it, such as Gemini. For a lecture or meeting, generate a transcript with a speech-to-text tool, then ask ChatGPT for a summary, chapter timestamps or quiz questions. I built live speech-to-text into my OCR &amp; Speech Workspace for exactly this reason: once speech is text, every search and summary tool works on it. For visual questions, export frames at the moments that matter and upload them as images. In the mobile app, voice mode with the camera can look at what you show it live, which helps for quick visual questions. Can you send ChatGPT videos? You can attach some files, but a video upload is not the same as video understanding. What ChatGPT can do with an attached video depends on the tools available in your plan, and long clips are rarely handled well. In practice, ChatGPT may be able to process a short file with its code tool, for example extracting frames or metadata with Python, then look at those frames. It will not reliably watch a long video and answer about every scene. Sending a link to a YouTube video does not help either: unless browsing can read a transcript, it sees the page, not the footage. Send the transcript plus key frames instead, and say exactly what you need from them. Can Claude AI edit videos? No. Claude works with text, images and documents such as PDFs, not video files, so it cannot cut or render video. Like ChatGPT, it is useful for scripts, transcripts, captions and the code that drives editing tools. Claude is strong at turning a rough transcript into a tight script, writing subtitles in SRT format, and producing ffmpeg or Python commands for repetitive edits such as batch trimming or adding a watermark. Developers also use it to write programmatic video code, for example a Remotion project where each scene is a React component rendered to MP4. Analyse footage the same way as with ChatGPT: a transcript plus selected frames as images. Can ChatGPT edit videos for YouTube? It cannot cut your YouTube video, but it can do most of the work around it: script, hook, title, description, chapter timestamps, tags, thumbnail concepts and a pinned comment. A workflow that saves hours: Write the script with ChatGPT, then read it aloud and rewrite anything you would not say. Record, edit in your editor, and export a transcript with timestamps. Ask ChatGPT for chapters from the transcript, three title options and a description that opens with the main point. Generate thumbnail ideas, then design the final thumbnail yourself so your face and text stay sharp. Watch retention, not the assistant's opinion, to judge what works. What are free AI tools like ChatGPT? Google Gemini, Anthropic's Claude, Microsoft Copilot, Perplexity, Meta AI, DeepSeek and Mistral's Le Chat are general AI assistants with free tiers. All of them chat, write and explain code, and most read images and documents. Each has a strength. Gemini fits into Gmail, Docs and Android and handles video input well. Claude is careful with long documents and code. Copilot is built into Windows, Edge and Microsoft 365. Perplexity answers with sources from a live web search. Free tiers come with usage limits and sometimes older models, and the limits change often. Pick two, run the same real task, such as summarising your lecture notes, in both, and keep the one whose answer you would actually use.

# Can Gemini transcribe audio? Files, M4A, video, and ChatGPT or Copilot
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/can-gemini-transcribe-audio/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-23

Yes, Gemini can transcribe audio. Its models accept audio as input, so you can upload a recording in the Gemini app or send it through the Gemini API and ask for a transcript, with timestamps, speaker labels, a summary or a translation. It can also transcribe the audio track of a video. This page covers files and formats including M4A, video, how ChatGPT and Copilot handle transcription, how Gemini compares with GPT, which Gemini model to use for images, where Gemini is available, and practical examples. Can Gemini transcribe audio? Yes. Upload a recording or record directly, then ask Gemini to transcribe it. Because Gemini understands the content, you can ask for more than a transcript: clean it up, label speakers, summarise, list action items or translate. A good prompt: "Transcribe this recording verbatim with timestamps every minute and label speakers as Speaker 1 and Speaker 2. Then give a five-bullet summary." Check names, numbers and technical terms, the most common errors in any transcription. For very long recordings, the API handles large files better than the app, and dedicated speech-to-text services offer features such as guaranteed verbatim output and streaming. I built live speech-to-text into my OCR &amp; Speech Workspace for this reason: transcripts turn speech into something you can search and summarise. Can Gemini transcribe audio files? Yes. In the Gemini app, attach the audio file and ask for a transcript. Through the Gemini API, upload the file with the Files API and pass it with your prompt. Common formats such as MP3, WAV, AAC, FLAC and OGG are supported. Using the API from Python: from google import genai client = genai.Client() audio = client.files.upload(file=&quot;lecture.mp3&quot;) resp = client.models.generate_content( model=&quot;gemini-2.5-flash&quot;, contents=[&quot;Transcribe this lecture with timestamps.&quot;, audio]) print(resp.text) There are limits on file size and total audio length per request; the audio documentation lists them. Split very long recordings into parts and combine the transcripts. Can Gemini transcribe M4A audio? M4A files contain AAC audio, which Gemini generally handles, but uploads of the M4A container itself sometimes fail depending on where you upload. If that happens, convert the file to MP3 or WAV, which work reliably. Also asked as: can gemini transcribe audio m4a Convert with one ffmpeg command: ffmpeg -i recording.m4a -ac 1 -ar 16000 recording.mp3 That also reduces the file to mono at 16 kHz, which is plenty for speech and makes uploads faster. Phone voice memos are often M4A, so this is a common fix. If you do not use the command line, many free audio converters do the same thing; avoid uploading private recordings to unknown converter websites. Can Gemini transcribe audio from a video? Yes. Gemini accepts video files and YouTube links in many cases, and can transcribe the speech, describe what is shown, and give timestamps. You can also extract the audio and send only that, which is faster and uses less of your limits. Also asked as: can gemini transcribe audio from video To extract audio: ffmpeg -i talk.mp4 -vn -ac 1 -ar 16000 talk.mp3 Then ask for a transcript or chapter list. When you need both speech and visuals, such as a lecture where slides matter, send the video and ask Gemini to note slide titles alongside the transcript. For YouTube videos with captions, those captions may already be a good starting transcript. Can ChatGPT transcribe audio? Yes, in several ways. ChatGPT transcribes your voice input when you dictate, voice mode understands speech in conversation, and uploaded audio can be transcribed depending on the tools and limits of your plan. OpenAI's API offers dedicated transcription models. For reliable transcripts of files, developers use OpenAI's speech-to-text API or the open-source Whisper model, which runs locally for free. In the ChatGPT app, short recordings work best; long meetings are better handled by a transcription tool, with ChatGPT then summarising the transcript. As with Gemini, check names and numbers. Do not upload recordings of other people without their consent. Will Copilot transcribe audio? Microsoft's tools transcribe audio, though not always through the Copilot chat itself. Teams transcribes meetings live, Word's Transcribe feature turns uploaded recordings into text with speakers and timestamps, and Copilot can then summarise those transcripts. In Word for the web, use Dictate, then Transcribe, upload an audio file, and insert the transcript into your document. In Teams meetings, turn on transcription, and Copilot can answer questions about the meeting and create a recap. For other cases, generate a transcript with one of these tools or with Whisper, then paste it into Copilot for summaries and action items. Availability depends on your Microsoft 365 plan and organisation settings. Gemini vs GPT: which is better? Gemini and OpenAI's GPT models are close in overall quality, and leadership changes with each release. Gemini is strong on long, multimodal inputs such as audio and video and is built into Google's apps; GPT models power ChatGPT's broad ecosystem. For transcription and media work, Gemini's native audio and video input is an advantage. For writing, coding and general assistance, both are excellent, and the better choice depends on your tasks and tools. Developers should compare cost, speed, rate limits and features such as structured outputs for their own workload. Run the same five real tasks on both and keep the one whose answers need less fixing. Which Gemini version is best for image generation? Use Google's Gemini image models, the family nicknamed Nano Banana, for creating and editing images in conversation, and Google's Imagen models for high-quality text-to-image generation through the API. The newest versions are usually the best. Gemini's image models are good at editing existing photos with instructions, keeping a character consistent across images, and combining several images. Imagen focuses on generating high-quality images from text. In the Gemini app, image creation picks a model for you; in the API and AI Studio you choose. Check the image generation documentation for current model names, and label AI-generated images when they could be mistaken for real photos. Where is Gemini available? Gemini is available in most countries and in many languages, on the web, Android and iOS, and inside Google Workspace. Availability of some features, such as image generation, Gemini Live or specific integrations, varies by country, age and account type. In India, Gemini supports English and several Indian languages and is widely available on Android, where it is replacing Google Assistant on many phones. Some regions have limited or no access because of local regulation or Google's rollout decisions. Google's Gemini help centre lists supported countries and languages. Work and school accounts depend on the administrator enabling Gemini. If a feature is missing, check your account type, age settings and app version before assuming it is unavailable. What are some examples of using Gemini AI? People use Gemini to summarise long documents and videos, transcribe and summarise recordings, plan study schedules and trips, draft emails and reports, explain code, generate and edit images, and research topics with cited sources. Also asked as: examples gemini ai Examples to try: "Transcribe this voice note and turn it into a to-do list with deadlines." "Summarise this YouTube lecture into revision notes with timestamps." "Here is my project report; point out unclear sections and missing evidence." "Plan a one-week revision schedule for these five subjects." "Explain this error and the fix, step by step." "Edit this photo to a plain white background for my resume." Check facts and names in every output before relying on it.

# Can you make AI? Building an AI as a beginner, and making AI images and videos
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/can-you-make-ai/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-23

Yes, you can make AI. As a beginner, the fastest route is to build an AI application on top of an existing model through an API, such as a chatbot that answers from your college notes; with some Python, you can also train small machine learning models yourself. You can also make AI images and videos with free tools. This page covers building your first AI, why learning AI and ML is worth it, and how to make AI photos and videos with ChatGPT, Gemini and Adobe Express, including what is free. Can you make your own AI? Yes. You can build AI applications by connecting to models such as Gemini, GPT or Claude through their APIs, and you can train your own smaller models with Python libraries such as scikit-learn and PyTorch. Training a large model like ChatGPT from scratch is beyond individuals. Three levels of "making AI": Use a model through an API: build a chatbot, summariser or document assistant. Hours to days. Train a small model: a spam classifier or image recogniser on your own data. Days. Fine-tune an open model: adapt a model to your task with LoRA on a single GPU. Days to weeks. Most real products are the first kind, done well. That is how I built RAG.NextUpgrad and DocuLens AI: existing models, with retrieval, validation and careful engineering around them. How do I make an AI as a beginner? Learn basic Python, get a free API key from Google AI Studio, and build one small, useful AI app: for example, a study assistant that answers questions from your notes and cites the page. A beginner path over a few weeks: Week 1: Python basics, variables, functions, lists and dictionaries. Week 2: call an LLM API and print a response; then add a simple web interface with Streamlit. Week 3: add your documents, split them into chunks and retrieve the relevant ones for each question. Week 4: deploy it for free and share it with friends for feedback. Alongside, do a short machine learning course to understand training and evaluation. Build first, then fill gaps in theory as you need it. Why learn AI and ML? Because AI and machine learning are becoming part of almost every software product and many non-technical jobs, and people who can build with AI are in demand. Learning them also teaches durable skills: data handling, statistics, programming and careful evaluation. Also asked as: why ai and ml For students, AI skills open roles such as AI engineer, ML engineer, data scientist and AI product developer, and make every other engineering role more productive. Even outside tech, knowing how models work helps you use them well and spot their mistakes. The field rewards builders: a student who ships one real AI project learns more than one who completes many courses. Start with a problem you care about, and let it pull you through the learning. Can you make AI images? Yes. Gemini, ChatGPT and Microsoft Copilot can all generate images from a text description for free within daily limits, and dedicated tools such as Adobe Firefly and Canva's AI features do the same. Also asked as: how to make an ai for beginners Write prompts with subject, setting, style, lighting and composition, for example "a flat illustration of students at a hackathon, laptops and sticky notes, bright colours, top-down view". Ask for changes in follow-up messages instead of starting over. For text inside images, such as posters, newer models do much better than older ones but still make mistakes, so check spelling. Respect copyright and trademarks: avoid generating logos or characters you do not own, and label AI images when they could mislead. Can you make AI photos? Yes. You can generate realistic photos from text, and edit your own photos with AI: change the background, adjust lighting, extend the frame, remove objects or apply a style. Gemini, ChatGPT, Adobe and many phone apps offer these features. For edits, upload the photo and describe the change precisely, such as "replace the background with a plain light grey studio wall, keep the person unchanged". Faces can shift slightly in AI edits, so check carefully before using images for anything official; never use AI edits for ID or passport photos. Never generate or edit photos of real people in ways they have not agreed to. Many tools add visible or invisible watermarks to mark AI images, which is a good thing for trust. Can you make AI videos? Yes. Text-to-video and image-to-video models, such as OpenAI's Sora, Google's Veo, Adobe Firefly and others, generate short clips from a prompt or a still image. Longer videos are built by editing several clips together. Generated clips are short, so plan a video as a sequence of shots. Describe each shot like a director: subject, action, setting, camera movement, lighting, style and sound. Expect to generate several takes and choose the best. For explainer or tutorial videos, real screen recordings and your own voice usually work better than generated footage, with AI clips as B-roll. Label AI-generated video when you publish it, and check your platform's rules on disclosure. Can you make AI videos for free? Partly. Free options exist but come with tight limits, watermarks or short clip lengths. Some apps offer a few free generations a day, and video editors such as Clipchamp, CapCut and Adobe Express include free AI features. Ways to make AI-assisted videos without paying: Write the script with a free chatbot and record your own voice and screen. Generate images for scenes for free, then animate them with simple pans and zooms in a free editor. Use free daily credits in video generation tools for a few key shots. Use free text-to-speech for narration, labelled as synthetic where relevant. Free offers change frequently, so check each tool's current plan page. Can you make AI videos with ChatGPT? ChatGPT itself writes, plans and creates images, while video generation comes from OpenAI's Sora, available through its own app and website for eligible users and regions. ChatGPT can still produce scripts, storyboards and prompts for Sora. A workflow: ask ChatGPT for a 30-second script and a shot list, then turn each shot into a detailed Sora prompt, generate the clips, and edit them together with narration and captions in a video editor. ChatGPT can also write ffmpeg commands to assemble images into a slideshow video. Availability and limits for Sora depend on your plan and country and have changed since launch, so check OpenAI's current information. Can you make AI videos on Gemini for free? Video generation in Gemini, powered by Google's Veo models, has mainly been part of paid Google AI plans with daily limits, though Google has run trials and student offers. Free accounts can still use Gemini to plan videos and generate images. If you have access, choose the video option in Gemini, write a detailed scene description and generate a short clip with sound. Without access, use Gemini for scripts, shot lists and still images, then assemble a video in a free editor. Google has offered free plan periods to eligible students in some countries, including India, so check the official Gemini pages for current offers. Generated videos carry Google's SynthID watermark. Can you make AI videos with Adobe Express? Yes. Adobe Express includes AI features powered by Adobe Firefly, including generating short video clips from text prompts, plus templates, animation, captions and editing tools to turn them into finished social videos. Adobe Express is beginner-friendly: pick a template, generate or add clips, add text and music, and export for Instagram, YouTube Shorts or presentations. Free accounts get limited generative credits, and paid plans include more. Adobe trains Firefly on licensed and public-domain content and positions it as designed for commercial use, which matters for business projects; still, read the current terms. As with any AI video, review the output for errors and label it where appropriate.

# Career after BCA: options, opportunities, and choosing the right path
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/career-after-bca/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-23

A career after BCA can go in several directions: a software or IT job, an MCA or other master's degree, a specialised path such as data science, AI or cybersecurity, government and banking exams, or building a startup. BCA is a solid base, and what you do during the three years decides which doors open. I completed my BCA at VSICS from 2023 to 2026 while shipping five production AI applications and leading engineering at SCULT INDIA, so this page combines the options with practical advice on building a career during the course, choosing a path, and admissions. What are the career options after BCA? The main options after BCA are a job in software development, web and app development, data analysis, testing, IT support or cloud; higher studies such as MCA, MBA or an MSc; specialised programmes in data science, AI or cybersecurity; government and banking jobs; and entrepreneurship. Also asked as: what is career after bca How they compare: Job right away: start earning and learning; best if you have projects and an internship. MCA: deepens computer science and improves eligibility for some recruiters and roles. MBA: suits product, business analysis or management interests, usually better after some work experience. Specialisations: data science, AI, cloud or security through courses and projects. Government exams: open to graduates from any stream. Startup or freelancing: if you have a real problem to solve and the appetite for risk. Is BCA a good career option? Yes, if you treat it as a foundation and build real skills alongside it. BCA gives you programming and computer applications from year one, costs less and takes less time than a BTech, and leads to the same software roles when you can show what you have built. Also asked as: is bca good career option Its limits are real: some mass recruiters prefer BTech or MCA, and campus placements vary widely by college. You overcome that with a portfolio: two or three deployed projects, internships, hackathons and a clean GitHub. The degree opens the door to interviews; skills get you through them. If you want pure engineering roles at core hardware companies or certain government technical posts, check eligibility, as some require an engineering degree. How do I make a career in BCA? Use the three years deliberately: master fundamentals and one programming language, build projects that match a target role, get at least one internship, join a community and hackathons, and prepare for interviews before final year. Also asked as: how to make career in bca A year-by-year plan: Year 1: Python or Java, Git, SQL and one small deployed project. Year 2: data structures, web development or data skills, a first hackathon, a community role. Year 3: one serious project in your target area, an internship, interview practice, applications. This is the roadmap I gave first-years at the VSICS induction seminar in July 2025: foundations and AI tools first, then hackathons and internships, then placements or a startup. Consistency across three years beats a last-semester rush. How do I choose a career after BCA? Test before you commit. Try short projects, internships or courses in two or three areas that interest you, notice what you enjoy and where you get good feedback, then choose the path that combines interest, ability and demand. Also asked as: how to choose career after bca Questions that help: Which projects did you finish without being forced to? Do you prefer building products, analysing data, solving security puzzles or managing people? What do job listings in that area ask for, and how far are you from it? Do you need to earn immediately, or can you study further? Talk to people two to five years ahead of you in each path. Their honest account of daily work is more useful than any ranking of "best careers". What are the career options in the BCA course itself? During the BCA course, you can already work in ways that build a career: internships, freelance web or app projects, teaching assistant or tutoring roles, open-source contributions, hackathons, community leadership and content creation about what you learn. Also asked as: bca course career options These count as experience on a resume and in interviews. Freelance work for local businesses teaches client communication, deadlines and deployment. Tutoring sharpens fundamentals. Hackathons build teamwork and give stories for interviews; three first prizes and a top-three finish shaped my own path. Choose one or two activities and do them well rather than ten superficially. What career opportunities does a BCA open? A BCA opens roles across IT services, product companies, startups, banking and fintech, e-commerce, government and education, in positions such as software developer, web developer, data analyst, QA engineer, support engineer, cloud associate and, with the right projects, junior AI engineer. Also asked as: bca course career opportunities Opportunities grow with specialisation. Students who add strong skills in an area, such as building RAG applications, cloud deployment or data analysis, compete for better roles. Remote work and freelancing for international clients are also open to skilled BCA graduates. Postgraduate study widens options further: MCA for deeper technical roles, MBA for management and product, and data science programmes for analytics careers. How does the BCA course prepare you for a career? The BCA course teaches programming, databases, operating systems, networks, web development and software engineering, plus a final project, which together form the base for software roles. It does not, by itself, teach deployment, real-world teamwork or how to present your work. Also asked as: bca course career Fill the gaps yourself: learn Git and GitHub early, deploy every project, write READMEs, use AI tools well while understanding their output, and practise explaining your work. Treat the final-year project as a portfolio piece: choose a real problem, ship it, measure something, and document it. Employers judge the project, not the marksheet line that says you completed one. What is the best BCA college through CUET? There is no single best college for everyone. Many central and state universities and their colleges admit BCA students through CUET; compare them on faculty, labs, internships, placement records for BCA specifically, location and fees. How to compare: Check the list of participating universities and programmes on the official CUET website for your year. Look for the BCA programme's own placement and internship data, not the university average. Ask current students about teaching quality, labs and coding culture. Check whether clubs, hackathons and communities are active. Confirm UGC recognition and the programme structure, three or four years. A college with an active tech community often matters more for your career than its name. When does BCA college start? BCA classes in India usually start between July and September, depending on the university's admission process, CUET results and counselling schedule. Private colleges admitting on class 12 marks may start earlier. Also asked as: when bca college will start · where is bca college Use the gap after class 12 well: learn basic Python, create a GitHub account, and build one tiny project, such as a calculator or a to-do app. Join an online community and follow a free course. Students who arrive with a little momentum find the first semester much easier and have more time later for projects, hackathons and internships. Check your university's academic calendar for exact dates. Where can you study BCA? You can study BCA at central, state and private universities and their affiliated colleges across India, as well as at autonomous colleges, and through recognised distance and online programmes from approved universities. Check that the university is recognised by the UGC and, for online or distance programmes, that it is approved to offer them. Compare the syllabus, practical labs, internship support and placement records. Location matters for internships and networking, but remote work and online communities have reduced that gap. Whatever college you choose, the projects, skills and network you build during the three years will matter most for your career.

# What is ChatGPT Business, ChatGPT Classic, and the best ChatGPT for students?
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/chatgpt-business-classic-students/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-23

ChatGPT Business is OpenAI's plan for teams and small organisations, with a shared workspace, admin controls and business data kept out of model training by default. ChatGPT Classic is a custom GPT made by OpenAI that gives you a plain chat model without extra tools. This page explains both, how ChatGPT compares with Google search, how students can get the most from it, which model suits writing, what a hallucination looks like, and how to write custom instructions that make every answer more useful. What is ChatGPT Business? ChatGPT Business, formerly called ChatGPT Team, is OpenAI's plan for teams. It gives each member ChatGPT with higher limits, plus a shared workspace, admin console, single sign-on and connectors to work tools. The main reasons organisations choose it over personal accounts are control and data protection: admins manage who has access, which features and connectors are allowed, and the workspace's data is not used to train OpenAI's models by default. Teams can share custom GPTs and projects. It suits startups, agencies, college departments and small companies. Large organisations with stricter compliance needs usually choose ChatGPT Enterprise. Plan features change, so check OpenAI's pricing page for the current comparison. How does ChatGPT Business work? An admin creates a workspace, invites members by email or single sign-on, and sets policies. Each member then uses ChatGPT as usual, but inside the workspace, with shared GPTs, projects and connected apps available to the team. Admins see a console for managing seats, billing, domain verification, connector permissions and data retention settings. Members can build custom GPTs for team workflows, such as a proposal writer that follows the company template, and share them only within the workspace. Connectors let ChatGPT search approved sources such as Google Drive, SharePoint or GitHub with each user's own permissions. Personal accounts stay separate, so a member's private chats are not mixed with the workspace. Before using it for client data, check your contracts and the workspace's data settings. What is ChatGPT Classic? ChatGPT Classic is a custom GPT published by OpenAI in the GPT store. It gives you a chat model without the extra capabilities of standard ChatGPT, such as web browsing, image generation or code execution. Some people prefer it for focused writing or reasoning tasks where they do not want the assistant searching the web or calling tools, and for a cleaner, more predictable conversation. You open it from the GPTs section by searching for "ChatGPT Classic". It still follows your custom instructions and the usual usage limits. Because GPT store listings change, check whether it is available and which model it currently uses on your account. What is the difference between ChatGPT and ChatGPT Classic? Standard ChatGPT can choose tools during a conversation: search the web, run code, analyse files, generate images and use memory. ChatGPT Classic is a plain conversational model without those tools. That makes Classic predictable but limited. It cannot look up current information, so its knowledge ends at the model's training data, and it cannot calculate with code or produce files. Standard ChatGPT is better for most tasks, especially research, data analysis and anything recent. Classic can be useful when you want pure writing or brainstorming without the model deciding to browse, or when comparing how a model answers from its own knowledge alone. ChatGPT vs Google: which should I use? Use Google to find specific pages, official sources, recent news, prices, local results and exact facts. Use ChatGPT to explain concepts, compare options, summarise, draft and solve problems step by step. They work best together. Google points you to sources; ChatGPT synthesises an answer, sometimes with sources if search is on. The risk with ChatGPT is a confident answer with no reliable source; the risk with Google is spending time sifting through pages. A good workflow: ask ChatGPT to explain a topic and list what to verify, then use Google to check the key facts on official or primary sources. For exam dates, admission rules, laws and medical information, always go to the official site. Google itself now shows AI summaries, so the line between them is blurring. What is the best ChatGPT for students? For most students, the free ChatGPT plan with good prompts is the best start. Use it as a tutor rather than an answer machine, and upgrade only if limits regularly block your study. Also asked as: how chatgpt helps students Ways to make it a tutor: Ask it to explain step by step and then quiz you, instead of giving answers outright. Use the study or tutoring mode if your plan offers one, which guides you through problems with questions. Create a Project for each subject with your syllabus and notes. Paste your own answer and ask for marking against a rubric. Check your college's rules on AI use in assignments; submitting generated work as your own can count as misconduct. How does ChatGPT help students? ChatGPT helps students understand concepts faster, practise with instant feedback, organise study plans, improve writing and debug code. The benefit comes when you use it to learn, not to skip learning. Practical uses: "Explain normalisation in databases with an example from a college library system." "Give me ten questions on operating systems scheduling, one at a time, and grade my answers." "Make a two-week revision timetable for these five subjects with these exam dates." "Here is my paragraph; point out unclear sentences but do not rewrite it." "Why does this Python code give a KeyError?" I tell first-year students the same thing in sessions: use AI tools early, but build the foundations yourself, because interviews and projects test what you understand. Which ChatGPT model is best for writing? For most writing, the default model is excellent. For long, structured pieces such as reports, research summaries or technical documentation, a reasoning or thinking mode can organise arguments better. The prompt matters more than the model. Good writing prompts state the audience, purpose, tone, length and structure, and include your own notes or draft. Ask for an outline first, agree on it, then write section by section. To keep your own voice, give ChatGPT a sample of your writing and ask it to edit lightly. For creative writing, try several drafts and combine the best parts. Always fact-check, because fluent writing can hide wrong claims. What is an example of a ChatGPT hallucination? A classic example is invented citations: ask for research papers on a topic and ChatGPT may list plausible titles, authors and journals that do not exist. In a well-known 2023 US case, lawyers were sanctioned after filing a brief with court cases a chatbot had made up. Also asked as: example chatgpt hallucination Other common hallucinations: wrong dates or numbers stated confidently, a library function that does not exist, a quote attributed to the wrong person, or details about a small company or person that sound right but are invented. Hallucinations happen because the model generates the most plausible text, not verified facts. Reduce them by turning on search, asking for sources and opening them, asking "how confident are you and what should I verify?", and checking code by running it. What is an example of ChatGPT custom instructions? Custom instructions tell ChatGPT who you are and how you want answers, so you do not repeat context in every chat. Here is an example for a computer science student: Also asked as: example chatgpt custom instructions About me: second-year BCA student in India. I know Python and basic SQL, learning web development with Next.js and FastAPI. How to respond: explain like a patient senior. Give a short answer first, then details. Use examples in Python. For code, explain each part briefly. When I ask about facts, say what I should verify. Do not write my assignments; help me understand and check my work. Keep instructions short and specific, update them as your goals change, and test them on a few typical questions to see whether answers improve.

# Why does ChatGPT pick 73? Plus: is ChatGPT Plus worth it, and why it is slow
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/chatgpt-picks-73-plus-and-speed/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-23

ChatGPT picks 73, 17, 37 or 42 when you ask for a random number because language models predict the most likely next token, and in human writing those numbers are the ones people choose when they try to sound random. The model is reproducing our bias, not rolling dice. This page also covers ChatGPT Plus: whether you can get it free, what it offers, how it compares with Go and Pro, whether to buy it, and why ChatGPT can be slow on your laptop or get slower during a chat. Why does ChatGPT pick 73? Because it is predicting what a person would most likely write, not generating randomness. In human text, "random" picks cluster on numbers that feel random, such as those ending in 7 and odd primes like 37 and 73, and the model learned that pattern. When you ask "pick a number between 1 and 100", the model assigns a probability to every possible answer. Training on human writing, plus tuning to give confident answers, concentrates that probability on a few favourites. Sampling at the default temperature then picks one of those favourites most of the time. Ask in a fresh chat and you will often see the same few numbers. That is a useful reminder of how these models work: they produce the most plausible text, which is not the same as the most correct or most random. Why does ChatGPT always pick 17? For a 1 to 20 range, 17 plays the same role 73 plays for 1 to 100: it is the number people most often name when asked for a random one, so it dominates the model's predictions. Humans avoid round numbers and the edges of a range, and odd primes feel "more random". If you need real randomness, do not ask the model to imagine it. Ask ChatGPT to run code instead, for example "use Python's random module to pick a number from 1 to 100", which uses a pseudo-random generator rather than the model's preferences. In your own apps, generate random values in code and pass them to the model if needed. The same lesson applies to anything that must be unbiased, such as shuffling a list, sampling test data or choosing a winner: use code, then let the model explain the result. Where is ChatGPT Plus free? ChatGPT Plus is a paid plan and is not generally free in any country. OpenAI has run limited promotions, for example offers for students in some markets, and in India it offered ChatGPT Go, a lighter paid plan, free for a period to eligible users. Also asked as: where chatgpt plus is free Promotions are announced by OpenAI and claimed inside ChatGPT or through official partners, never through third-party sites. Beware of "free Plus" offers that ask for your login, sell shared accounts or require an app download: they risk your account and your data, and shared accounts break OpenAI's terms. The free tier is also more capable than many people assume, with access to strong models within limits, so try it seriously before paying. What does ChatGPT Plus offer? ChatGPT Plus offers higher usage limits than the free tier, access to more capable models and reasoning modes, and more use of features such as deep research, image generation, advanced voice, file analysis, agent mode and Codex. The practical gain is fewer interruptions: on the free tier you can run out of the best model and fall back to a lighter one, while Plus lets you work with stronger models for longer. Exact limits and the feature list change often, so check OpenAI's pricing page for the current details. Plus is an individual plan; teams use business plans with admin controls and data protections. Should I buy ChatGPT Plus? Buy it if the free tier's limits regularly interrupt work that matters to you, such as daily coding, research or writing, and the time saved is worth the cost. If you use ChatGPT a few times a week for quick questions, the free tier is enough. A simple test: for two weeks, note every time the free tier blocked you or gave a weaker answer that cost you time. If it happens daily, Plus is likely worth it. Also compare the alternatives: Go if you mostly need higher limits on everyday tasks, and the free tiers of Claude, Gemini and Copilot, which you can combine at no cost. For students, the biggest improvement usually comes from better prompts and checking answers, not from a paid plan. What is the difference between ChatGPT Go and Plus? ChatGPT Go is a lower-cost paid plan with higher limits than the free tier for everyday features such as messages, image generation and file uploads. Plus adds access to more capable models and reasoning modes, more advanced features and higher limits again. Go was launched first in India and then expanded to other countries, aimed at people who use ChatGPT daily but do not need the most advanced models or agent features. Plus suits people who need deep research, stronger reasoning, agent mode or Codex regularly. Because OpenAI adjusts what each plan includes, compare them on the official pricing page for your country before choosing. What is the difference between ChatGPT Plus and Pro? Pro is the top individual plan for very heavy professional use. It has much higher limits than Plus and access to OpenAI's most capable reasoning modes, with priority access to new features. Plus is the mainstream paid plan. Choose Pro only if you hit Plus limits constantly on work that earns money, or you need the strongest reasoning for hard technical, scientific or analytical problems every day. For almost every student and most developers, Plus is the sensible ceiling. Pro does not make ChatGPT infallible; it gives more capacity and the strongest models, but you still need to verify answers. Why is ChatGPT slow? ChatGPT is slow when OpenAI's servers are under heavy load, when you use a reasoning model that thinks before answering, or when your conversation is very long. Network problems and browser issues add to it. Also asked as: why chatgpt is slow Check these first: Status: OpenAI's status page shows outages and degraded performance. Model: reasoning modes spend seconds to minutes thinking on purpose; use a faster mode for simple tasks. Peak hours: responses slow when many users are active, and free-tier users feel it first. Chat length: very long chats take longer to process and render. Network: VPNs, proxies and weak Wi-Fi delay streaming responses. If only one chat is slow, start a new one with a short summary of the earlier context. Why is ChatGPT so slow on my laptop? Usually because the browser tab is struggling, not the AI. Very long conversations with code blocks and images create a heavy page, and extensions, low memory or an outdated browser make it worse. Fixes that work: Start a new chat; long chats are the most common cause. Close other heavy tabs and apps to free memory. Disable extensions, especially ad blockers and page modifiers, or try a private window. Update the browser, or try the ChatGPT desktop app. Clear the site's cache and cookies if the page behaves oddly. Turn off a VPN or switch networks to rule out connection issues. If ChatGPT is fast on your phone but slow on your laptop, the problem is local to the laptop's browser. Why does ChatGPT slow down during a conversation? Because every reply processes the whole conversation so far. As a chat grows, the model has more text to read before answering, and the browser has more messages to render, so each response takes longer. Long chats also get worse, not only slower: early instructions can be lost or weakened when the context is very long, and the model may mix up details from different parts of the conversation. Keep one chat per task. When a chat gets long, ask ChatGPT for a short summary of decisions and facts, copy it into a new chat, and continue there. For ongoing projects, use a Project in ChatGPT with files and instructions, so you do not need one endless chat.

# Which ChatGPT version is best, who created it, and why it keeps freezing
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/chatgpt-versions-and-freezing/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-23

The best ChatGPT version for most people is the default model ChatGPT picks for you, with a reasoning or thinking mode for hard problems; the specific model names change every few months. ChatGPT was created by OpenAI, launched in November 2022, and built by pre-training a GPT model on large amounts of text and then training it to follow instructions with human feedback. This page also explains ChatGPT Enterprise, what you get without paying, practical uses, and how to fix ChatGPT freezing in Chrome or on a Mac, and Cursor freezing too. Which ChatGPT version is best? For everyday tasks, the default model in ChatGPT is the best balance of speed and quality. For hard maths, complex code, data analysis or careful planning, use the reasoning or thinking option, which takes longer but makes fewer mistakes. OpenAI now routes many requests automatically, sending simple questions to fast models and hard ones to reasoning models, so manual model picking matters less than it did. Rules of thumb: use a fast mode for rewriting, summarising and quick facts; use thinking for anything with several steps where a wrong step is costly; use deep research when you need a cited report from many sources. Model names and availability per plan change often, so check the model picker in your account rather than lists online. Who is the founder of ChatGPT? ChatGPT was created by OpenAI, the AI research company founded in December 2015 by a group that included Sam Altman, Greg Brockman, Ilya Sutskever, Wojciech Zaremba, John Schulman and Elon Musk. Sam Altman is OpenAI's chief executive. Also asked as: who chatgpt founder No single person invented ChatGPT; it was built by OpenAI's research and engineering teams on years of earlier work, including the transformer architecture published by Google researchers in 2017 and OpenAI's own GPT models from 2018 onwards. Elon Musk left OpenAI's board in 2018. Microsoft became OpenAI's major partner and investor, which is why Microsoft's Copilot products use OpenAI models. How was ChatGPT created? ChatGPT was created in two broad stages: pre-training a large GPT language model on a huge body of text to predict the next word, then fine-tuning it to follow instructions and hold conversations, using examples written by people and reinforcement learning from human feedback. Also asked as: how chatgpt created In the feedback stage, human reviewers ranked several model answers to the same prompt; a reward model learned those preferences, and the language model was trained to produce answers the reward model scored highly. OpenAI described this method in its 2022 paper on InstructGPT, ChatGPT's predecessor. ChatGPT launched as a research preview on 30 November 2022 and reached a very large user base within weeks. Since then OpenAI has added newer models, reasoning modes, tools such as search and code execution, voice, images and memory. What is ChatGPT Enterprise? ChatGPT Enterprise is OpenAI's plan for large organisations. It adds enterprise security and admin controls, single sign-on, data that is not used to train OpenAI's models by default, higher limits, and connectors to company tools. Organisations choose it so employees can use ChatGPT on work data without the risks of personal accounts: admins manage users, set which features and connectors are allowed, and see usage analytics, while compliance features help meet company policies. Smaller teams use the business plan with similar protections. For students, the relevant point is that the ChatGPT you use at an internship may have different features and rules from your personal account, so read the company's AI policy before pasting anything into it. How does ChatGPT treat you without premium? Free users get the same core ChatGPT with capable models, but with lower limits. When you hit a limit, ChatGPT falls back to a lighter model or asks you to wait, and some advanced features are limited or unavailable. Also asked as: how chatgpt treats you without premium On the free tier you can chat, search the web, upload files and images, use voice and create images within limits. What you notice is rationing: the strongest model and features such as deep research run out sooner, and responses may slow at peak times. Quality on simple tasks is very similar. Make the free tier go further with one clear, complete prompt instead of many follow-ups, new chats per task, and the fast model for simple work. What are some examples of using ChatGPT? People use ChatGPT to explain concepts, write and edit text, write and debug code, analyse data and documents, plan projects, practise interviews and languages, and brainstorm ideas. Also asked as: chatgpt examples of use Examples that work well for students and developers: "Explain recursion with a real-life analogy, then give me three practice problems." "Here is my error and the code around it. What is wrong and how do I fix it?" "Turn these lecture notes into a one-page summary and ten quiz questions." "Review my resume against this job description and list the gaps." "Act as an interviewer for a junior Python developer role and grade my answers." "Analyse this CSV and plot monthly totals." Check facts and run code before relying on it. Why does ChatGPT keep freezing? ChatGPT usually freezes because the conversation is very long, the browser is short of memory, an extension interferes with the page, or OpenAI's service is having problems. Starting a new chat fixes most cases. Work through these: Check OpenAI's status page for incidents. Start a new chat and paste a short summary of the old one. Close other heavy tabs and apps. Try a private window to rule out extensions. Update the browser or use the desktop app. Switch networks or turn off a VPN. If freezing happens only in one chat with lots of code blocks or images, that chat has simply become too heavy for the page to render smoothly. Why does ChatGPT keep freezing on Chrome? On Chrome, freezing usually comes from a very long chat, an extension such as an ad blocker or grammar checker modifying the page, too many open tabs using memory, or a corrupted site cache. Fixes for Chrome: Open ChatGPT in an Incognito window; if it works, disable extensions one by one. Clear cookies and cached data for chatgpt.com from site settings. Update Chrome and restart it. Check that hardware acceleration is on in Chrome's system settings. Use Chrome's task manager to see whether the ChatGPT tab uses unusual memory. If none of this helps, compare with another browser or the desktop app to see whether the problem is Chrome-specific. Why does ChatGPT keep freezing on my Mac? On a Mac, freezing usually comes from a very long conversation, low memory with many apps open, an outdated browser or ChatGPT app, or a browser extension. The same fixes apply: new chat, fewer apps, updates, no extensions. Specific steps: Update the ChatGPT Mac app, or your browser, and macOS. Open Activity Monitor and check memory pressure; quit heavy apps if it is high. If the desktop app freezes, quit it fully and reopen it, or sign out and back in. Try ChatGPT in Safari or Chrome to see whether the problem is the app or your account. Start a new chat for long-running work. Older Macs with limited memory struggle with very long chats full of code, so keeping conversations short helps most. Why does Cursor AI keep freezing? Cursor usually freezes while indexing a very large project, when heavy extensions run alongside it, when memory is short, or when the editor is out of date. Excluding big folders from indexing fixes most cases. Steps that help: Add a .cursorignore file listing folders such as node_modules, build outputs, datasets and logs, so Cursor does not index them. Update Cursor to the latest version. Disable extensions one at a time to find a misbehaving one. Close projects you are not using and check memory use. Open the developer tools or logs from the Help menu to see the actual error. If one long agent session hangs, stop it, start a new chat and give a smaller task.

# ChatGPT vs Copilot: the difference, and how to use Copilot in Teams
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/chatgpt-vs-copilot-teams/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-23

ChatGPT and Microsoft Copilot are both AI assistants, and Copilot runs largely on OpenAI's GPT models, but they are different products: ChatGPT is OpenAI's standalone app with its own tools, while Copilot is Microsoft's assistant built into Windows, Edge, Bing and Microsoft 365. The right choice depends on where your work lives. This page compares them, explains why Copilot sometimes seems weaker, and covers Copilot in Microsoft Teams: where to find it, how it works in chats and meetings, and where meeting transcripts are stored. ChatGPT vs Copilot: which should I use? Use Copilot when your work is in Microsoft 365, such as Outlook, Word, Excel and Teams, or your organisation provides it with data protection. Use ChatGPT as a broad assistant with custom GPTs, projects, memory, strong image generation and coding agents. Also asked as: when to use copilot vs chatgpt For a student, ChatGPT is often the more flexible learning and side-project companion, while Copilot is the natural choice inside a college or company Microsoft 365 account, where it can see your documents and meetings with your permissions. Many people use both: Copilot for work documents and meetings, ChatGPT for exploration and personal projects. Test both on three of your real tasks before deciding. Is Copilot the same as ChatGPT? No. They share technology, since Microsoft builds Copilot largely on OpenAI's models, but they are separate products from different companies, with different apps, features, integrations, accounts and privacy terms. Also asked as: is copilot and chatgpt the same Copilot adds Microsoft's own layers: grounding with Bing search, access to your Microsoft 365 data through Microsoft Graph for work accounts, enterprise data protection, and integration into Windows and Office. ChatGPT adds OpenAI's layers: custom GPTs, projects, memory, canvas, Codex and its app ecosystem. The same underlying model can therefore behave differently in each, because the instructions, tools and context around it differ. Do Copilot and ChatGPT use the same model? Often from the same family, but not necessarily the same version at the same time. Copilot uses OpenAI's GPT models hosted by Microsoft, along with Microsoft's own models and, in some features, models from other providers. ChatGPT uses OpenAI's latest models directly. Microsoft decides which model serves each Copilot request and does not always show it, while ChatGPT lets you choose between modes in many plans. New OpenAI models usually reach ChatGPT first or at the same time, and Microsoft adopts them on its own schedule after testing. In practice, differences in answers come as much from system instructions, safety settings and grounding as from the model version. When should I use Copilot vs ChatGPT? Use Copilot for tasks tied to Microsoft 365 content and Windows: summarising a Teams meeting, drafting a reply in Outlook, analysing an Excel table, or asking about your organisation's files. Use ChatGPT for open-ended learning, writing, coding, image work and anything outside Microsoft 365. Examples: "What did we decide in yesterday's project meeting?": Copilot in Teams. "Turn this Word report into a ten-slide deck": Copilot in PowerPoint. "Teach me recursion and quiz me": ChatGPT or Copilot both work. "Build a small web app with tests in my repository": ChatGPT's Codex or GitHub Copilot. "Generate and edit an illustration": ChatGPT. When company data is involved, use the tool your organisation has approved. Why is Copilot worse than ChatGPT? Copilot is not inherently worse, but it can feel that way because it may use faster models for some requests, applies more conservative instructions, and often lacks the context you assumed it had. Precise prompts and attached context close most of the gap. Common reasons and fixes: Missing context: open the document or attach the file before asking. Vague request: state the goal, audience, format and length. Wrong product: Microsoft 365 Copilot needs a licence for work data; free Copilot cannot see your work files. Search-heavy answers: Copilot often grounds in web results, which can make answers shorter and more cautious. For deep reasoning tasks, choose Copilot's deeper or thinking mode if available. Where do I find Copilot in Teams? In Microsoft Teams, Copilot appears in the left app bar or as Copilot Chat, in chats and channels as a Copilot button, and in meetings as a Copilot button in the meeting controls. Which ones you see depends on your licence and your organisation's settings. Also asked as: where to find copilot in teams · how copilot works in teams · how to copilot in teams Copilot Chat, available to many work and school accounts, is a general assistant grounded in the web and your uploaded files. The full Microsoft 365 Copilot licence adds Copilot inside chats, channels and meetings, with access to your Teams messages, files and meeting transcripts within your permissions. If you see no Copilot at all, check that Teams is updated and ask your IT team whether Copilot is enabled for your account. How does Copilot work in Teams? In Teams, Copilot uses a language model with access to the content you are allowed to see: chat and channel messages, files and meeting transcripts. It summarises conversations, answers questions about them and drafts messages. In a chat or channel, ask "summarise the last week of this conversation" or "what decisions were made about the launch date?", and Copilot answers with references to the messages. In meetings, it works from the live transcript. It respects permissions, so it will not reveal content from chats you are not part of. Like any assistant, it can misattribute who said what or miss nuance, so check important points against the transcript before acting on them. How do I use Copilot in Teams? Open a chat, channel or meeting and select the Copilot button, then ask in plain language: summarise, list action items, find what someone said, or draft a reply. You can also use Copilot Chat from the app bar for questions across your work content. Useful prompts: "Summarise the unread messages in this channel and highlight anything that needs my reply." "List the action items from this chat with owners and deadlines." "Draft a polite reply asking for the report by Friday." "What files were shared in this chat about the hackathon?" Be specific about time ranges and people. Copilot's drafts are starting points; edit them so they sound like you and contain only facts you can stand behind. How do I use Copilot in a Teams meeting? Turn on transcription when the meeting starts, then open Copilot from the meeting controls. During the meeting you can ask for a recap, open questions or action items; afterwards, the meeting recap shows notes and tasks generated from the transcript. Also asked as: how to copilot a teams meeting Organisers can also allow Copilot to work only during the meeting without keeping a transcript, depending on organisation settings, in which case after-meeting recaps are limited. Good prompts: "What have I missed in the last ten minutes?", "What are the unresolved questions?", and "Draft a follow-up email with decisions and owners." Tell participants when transcription is on; many organisations require it. Review the recap before sharing, because summaries can drop qualifications or merge points. Where are Copilot Teams transcripts stored? Meeting recordings and transcripts are stored in Microsoft 365 within your organisation's tenant, typically in the meeting organiser's OneDrive for regular meetings and in the channel's SharePoint site for channel meetings, governed by retention and access policies. Also asked as: where do copilot teams transcripts get stored Who can see a transcript depends on meeting settings and permissions, usually the organiser and attendees. Copilot reads the transcript to answer questions and build recaps, and Copilot interactions themselves are stored under the organisation's compliance settings. Admins control whether transcription is allowed, how long recordings and transcripts are kept, and who can download them. For sensitive meetings, check with the organiser before turning transcription on, and follow your organisation's data policy.

# ChatGPT vs Gemini: the difference, which is better, and when to use each
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/chatgpt-vs-gemini/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-23

ChatGPT and Gemini are both AI assistants that chat, answer questions, write, code and work with images and files. ChatGPT is made by OpenAI and runs on its GPT models; Gemini is made by Google and runs on its Gemini models. They are close in capability, and the better choice depends mostly on the task and on which ecosystem you already use. This page explains what each is, how they differ, which is better for what, when to use Claude instead, what this kind of tool is called, and why opinions online disagree so much. What are ChatGPT and Gemini? ChatGPT is OpenAI's AI assistant, launched in November 2022. Gemini is Google's AI assistant, launched as Bard in 2023 and renamed Gemini in early 2024. Both are chat interfaces built on large language models. Also asked as: gemini vs chatgpt reddit You talk to either in plain language by typing or speaking, and they respond with text, code, images or actions such as searching the web. Both have free tiers and paid plans, apps for phones and the web, and developer APIs. Under the hood, both are transformer-based models trained on large amounts of text, code, images and audio, then tuned to follow instructions and behave safely. They make similar kinds of mistakes, so the same verification habits apply to both. Are ChatGPT and Gemini the same? No. They are different products from different companies, built on different model families: GPT models from OpenAI and Gemini models from Google. They overlap heavily in what they do, but differ in strengths, features and integrations. The overlap is why people treat them as interchangeable for everyday tasks such as explanations, summaries and drafts, where both perform well. The differences show in the details: which tools each can use, how each connects to your other apps, how each handles very long documents or video, and how each phrases and structures answers. Your data also goes to different companies under different privacy terms, which matters for work and personal information. What is the difference between ChatGPT and Gemini? The biggest differences are ecosystem and features. Gemini is built into Google's products, such as Gmail, Docs, Drive, Android, Maps and YouTube. ChatGPT is a standalone assistant with its own ecosystem of custom GPTs, apps, projects, memory and coding tools. Practical differences that matter: Integration: Gemini works naturally with Google Workspace; ChatGPT connects to many services through connectors and apps. Media: Gemini handles video input natively through its API; ChatGPT offers strong image generation and voice. Coding: ChatGPT has Codex; Google has Gemini Code Assist and Antigravity. Plans: both have free tiers and paid plans with different bundles, such as Google's plans including cloud storage. Both change features often, so compare current versions. How is Gemini different from ChatGPT under the hood? Gemini models were designed from the start to handle text, images, audio and video together, and support very long context windows. GPT models also handle multiple types of input, with OpenAI pairing them with separate models for images, video and speech. Also asked as: how gemini is different from chatgpt Both families come in tiers: fast, cheaper models for everyday use and larger reasoning models for hard problems, and both apps route requests between them. Google grounds Gemini answers with Google Search, while ChatGPT uses its own search integration. The training data, model sizes and exact architectures are not public for either. For most users these differences show up indirectly, as speed, how well long files are handled, and how current the answers are. ChatGPT vs Gemini: which is better? Neither is better at everything. Both are top-tier assistants, and benchmark leadership changes with each model release. The better one for you is the one that gives better results on your actual tasks, in the apps you already use. Also asked as: chatgpt vs gemini which is better A fair test takes twenty minutes: pick five tasks you do often, such as explaining a concept, summarising a PDF, debugging code, drafting an email and planning a week, and run the same prompts in both. Judge accuracy, clarity and how much editing each answer needs. Many people end up using both: Gemini for anything inside Google Workspace and Android, ChatGPT for general work and its tool ecosystem. Public leaderboards, such as LMArena's community rankings, give a broad signal but not a verdict on your use case. When should I use ChatGPT vs Gemini? Use Gemini when your work lives in Google's ecosystem: Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Drive, YouTube, Maps or an Android phone. Use ChatGPT for a broad standalone assistant with custom GPTs, projects, memory, image generation and coding agents. Also asked as: when to use chatgpt vs gemini Examples: Summarise a long Gmail thread or a Drive folder: Gemini. Ask about a YouTube lecture or analyse a video file: Gemini. Build a reusable assistant for a repeated task: either, through custom GPTs or Gems. Generate and edit images in conversation: ChatGPT is very strong here. Work on a code repository with an agent: ChatGPT's Codex, or Google's coding tools. If your college uses Google Workspace, Gemini in your student account may be the most convenient. When should I use ChatGPT vs Claude vs Gemini? Use ChatGPT as a broad all-rounder, Gemini inside Google's ecosystem and for video and very long multimodal inputs, and Claude for long documents, careful writing and coding work, including Claude Code for real repositories. Also asked as: when to use chatgpt vs claude vs gemini This is a starting point, not a rule. All three are close enough that the prompt and the context you provide often matter more than the brand. For developers, the choice also depends on the API: pricing, rate limits, latency and features such as tool use or batch processing. In RAG.NextUpgrad I built multi-provider fallback, so the product keeps working when one provider is slow or down; that design also lets you switch models when one improves. Students can use the free tiers of all three and keep whichever helps most. How does Gemini AI compare to ChatGPT for students? For students, both are excellent and free tiers go a long way. Gemini is especially convenient with a Google account, Google Docs and YouTube lectures, and Google has run free plan offers for students. ChatGPT is strong as a tutor, writing coach and coding helper. Study tasks where each shines: Turning a recorded or YouTube lecture into notes: Gemini. Step-by-step tutoring and quizzes: both, with ChatGPT's study-style prompting a popular choice. Studying from your own notes and papers: Google's NotebookLM is excellent and free. Debugging programming assignments: both; check by running the code. Whatever you use, follow your college's rules on AI in assignments. What are ChatGPT, Gemini and Claude called? They are called AI chatbots or AI assistants, and more technically, applications built on large language models, or LLMs. Because they also handle images, audio and video, they are sometimes called multimodal AI assistants. Also asked as: what are chatgpt gemini claude called When they can take actions, such as browsing, running code or using apps to complete tasks, they are described as AI agents. The broader field is generative AI, since they generate new text, images, audio and code. Microsoft Copilot, Meta AI, Perplexity, DeepSeek and Mistral's Le Chat belong to the same category. In job descriptions, building products with these models is usually called GenAI engineering or AI engineering. Why do Reddit opinions on Gemini vs ChatGPT differ so much? Because people test different tasks, different model versions and different plans at different times. A comparison from a few months ago may describe models that have since been replaced, and one person's coding task says little about another's essay. Online threads are also shaped by strong feelings about companies, by free-tier users comparing against paid-tier users, and by single memorable failures. Treat them as a source of ideas for what to test, not as a verdict. Look for posts that state the exact model, plan, date and prompt, and ideally share the outputs. Then run your own small test: your tasks, your prompts, both tools, side by side. That answer is the only one that applies to you.
