# Chroma vs ChromaDB: what Chroma does in Python, examples and common errors
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/chroma-vector-database-python/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-23

Chroma, often called ChromaDB, is an open-source vector database for AI applications: it stores text chunks, their embeddings and metadata, and returns the most similar chunks for a query, which is the retrieval step in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). It is popular for prototypes because it runs inside Python with a few lines of code. This page covers the name, its role in LLM apps, Python usage and examples, avoiding repeated embedding costs, in-memory versus persistent storage, a common Docker crash, testing RAG with Chroma, and the unrelated colour term. What is the difference between Chroma and ChromaDB? There is no difference: Chroma is the project and company name, and ChromaDB is the common name for the database and its Python package, installed with pip install chromadb. Also asked as: chroma vs chromadb Chroma runs in several modes: embedded inside your Python process, as a client-server setup with a separate Chroma server, or as a hosted cloud service. Tutorials use "Chroma", "ChromaDB" and "Chroma DB" interchangeably. In LangChain and LlamaIndex, the integration is usually called Chroma. If you see "Chroma" in a photography or colour context, that is an unrelated meaning covered at the end of this page. What is ChromaDB in LLM applications? In LLM applications, ChromaDB is the vector store that holds your knowledge: document chunks with their embeddings. When a user asks a question, the app searches Chroma for similar chunks and passes them to the LLM so it can answer from your documents. Chroma provides collections, which are like tables, with documents, embeddings, metadata and IDs. It can compute embeddings for you with a default or chosen embedding function, or accept embeddings you compute yourself. Metadata filters let you restrict search, for example to one course or date range. It uses an approximate nearest-neighbour index, HNSW, for fast search. For many student projects and internal tools, Chroma is all the vector database you need. What does Chroma do in Python? In Python, Chroma lets you create collections, add documents with IDs and metadata, and query them by text or embedding to get the most similar items, all from a simple API that can run in-process without a separate server. Also asked as: what does chroma do python · how to use chroma db in python Typical operations: client.get_or_create_collection(name) to create or open a collection. collection.add(ids=..., documents=..., metadatas=...) to index chunks. collection.query(query_texts=[...], n_results=5, where={...}) to search with filters. collection.update, upsert and delete to keep data current. Results include IDs, documents, metadata and distances, which you pass to your LLM prompt with IDs for citations. How do I use ChromaDB in Python? Install chromadb, create a persistent client, create a collection, add documents with unique IDs, and query it. import chromadb client = chromadb.PersistentClient(path=&quot;./chroma_store&quot;) col = client.get_or_create_collection(&quot;notes&quot;) col.upsert( ids=[&quot;os-1&quot;, &quot;os-2&quot;], documents=[&quot;A process is a program in execution.&quot;, &quot;Paging divides memory into fixed-size pages.&quot;], metadatas=[{&quot;subject&quot;: &quot;os&quot;, &quot;page&quot;: 3}, {&quot;subject&quot;: &quot;os&quot;, &quot;page&quot;: 7}], ) res = col.query(query_texts=[&quot;what is paging?&quot;], n_results=1, where={&quot;subject&quot;: &quot;os&quot;}) print(res[&quot;documents&quot;][0], res[&quot;metadatas&quot;][0]) The default embedding function downloads a small model on first use; for production, choose your embedding model explicitly and use it consistently. What are some Chroma examples? Common Chroma examples are a chatbot over your PDFs, semantic search over notes or support tickets, a FAQ assistant for a college or product, and memory for an AI agent that stores past conversation summaries. Project ideas to practise: Study assistant: index lecture notes by page and answer questions with page citations. Support search: index past tickets and suggest similar resolved issues. Code search: embed function docstrings and search your codebase in plain language. Agent memory: store summaries of past tasks and retrieve them when relevant. Pair Chroma with keyword search for exact terms such as error codes, which embeddings often miss, and add a reranker when results look plausible but wrong. How do I avoid recomputing embeddings with Chroma? Use a persistent client so embeddings survive restarts, give each chunk a stable ID, and upsert only new or changed chunks, tracking a hash of each document to detect changes. Never rebuild the whole collection when one file changes. Also asked as: how to avoid re computation of embeddings with chroma A simple pattern: compute an ID such as docname#chunkindex and a content hash; before indexing, check which IDs already exist with the same hash; embed and upsert only those that are new or changed; delete IDs for removed content. If you compute embeddings yourself, cache them on disk keyed by content hash. Remember that changing the embedding model requires re-embedding everything, because vectors from different models are not comparable. Is it a problem to store a vector database in memory? For prototypes, tests and small datasets, in-memory storage is fine and fast. For anything users depend on, it is a problem: data disappears when the process restarts, memory limits cap your dataset, and multiple app instances cannot share it. Also asked as: is it a problem to store your vector database in memory Use in-memory clients for unit tests and notebooks, and persistent storage in development and production, with backups. If you run several app instances, use a client-server Chroma or a database such as PostgreSQL with pgvector, so all instances see the same data. Also keep your source documents as the true record: the vector index should be rebuildable from them, which makes recovery and model changes straightforward. Why does ChromaDB crash with "illegal instruction" in a Docker container? "Illegal instruction" usually means a compiled dependency, such as the HNSW index library or an ML runtime, was built for CPU instructions your machine or emulator does not support. It often happens when running an image built for a different CPU architecture, such as amd64 under emulation on an ARM Mac. Also asked as: why does chroma db crash with &quot;illegal instruction&quot; in this python:3.10-slim container Fixes to try: Run an image that matches your machine's architecture, or build the image natively on it. Avoid emulation for this workload where possible. Use the official Chroma server image and connect from your app as a client. Rebuild the dependency from source without CPU-specific optimisations, following Chroma's troubleshooting docs. Pin versions known to work on your platform. Check Chroma's GitHub issues for your exact error and platform; others usually hit it first. How do you test RAG memory with ChromaDB? Treat retrieval as testable code: create a fresh in-memory or temporary Chroma collection in each test, load a fixed set of documents, run known queries and assert that the expected IDs come back in the top results. Also asked as: how automating rag memory tests with chromadb quadrupled our bug discovery rate What to test: Retrieval correctness: expected chunk IDs appear in the top k for each query. Updates: changed documents replace old chunks; deleted ones disappear. Filters: metadata filters exclude what they should. Agent memory: stored summaries are retrieved in later turns and old ones expire as designed. Regressions: run the suite on every change to chunking or embeddings. Automated retrieval tests catch silent failures, such as duplicate chunks or broken updates, long before users notice wrong answers. What is colour chroma? In colour theory, chroma is the colourfulness or intensity of a colour relative to a neutral grey of the same brightness: high chroma colours are vivid, low chroma colours are muted or greyish. It is unrelated to the Chroma vector database. Chroma is one of the three dimensions in colour systems such as Munsell, alongside hue and value or lightness. "High chroma vs low chroma" comparisons appear in painting, design, photography and fashion; for example, a bright red is high chroma, while a dusty rose is low chroma. In photography, "chroma noise" refers to random colour speckles in images. If you came here for databases, the sections above cover ChromaDB.

# What is a Claude API key, and how do you get and set up the Claude API?
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/claude-api-key-setup/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-23

A Claude API key is a secret token that lets your own code call Claude models through Anthropic's API; requests made with it are billed to your developer account. You create keys in the Claude Console, store them in an environment variable, and use them with Anthropic's SDKs or plain HTTP. This page covers getting a key, the Console and developer platform, the docs, how the API differs from the claude.ai app, how a request works, setting it up in Python, using Claude in VS Code, and whether the API supports skills. What is a Claude API key? A Claude API key is a long secret string, beginning with sk-ant-, that authenticates requests to Anthropic's API. Anyone who has your key can make requests that are charged to your account, so it must be kept private. Also asked as: what is claude api key Keys belong to a workspace in your organisation in the Claude Console, so you can create separate keys for development and production, set spending limits per workspace, and revoke a key instantly if it leaks. A key is not your claude.ai login and does not give access to your chat history. Common leaks happen when keys are pasted into front-end JavaScript, committed to a public GitHub repository or shared in screenshots. Keep keys in environment variables or a secrets manager, and rotate any key you suspect has been exposed. How do I get a Claude AI API key? Sign up in the Claude Console, set up billing for your organisation, then open the API keys page and create a key. Copy it immediately; the Console shows the full key only once. Also asked as: how to claude ai api key · claude ai vs claude api The steps: Sign in to the Console with your email or Google account. Add billing details and purchase credits or set up payment, as the Console prompts. Go to API keys and choose "Create key", giving it a clear name such as "college-project-dev". Copy the key into a password manager or your project's .env file. A claude.ai Pro or Max subscription does not include API credits; the two are billed separately. Students should set a low spending limit while learning, so a bug in a loop cannot run up a large bill. Where is the Claude API Console? The Claude Console, previously called the Anthropic Console, is Anthropic's web dashboard for developers, linked from the Claude developer documentation. It is where you create keys, manage billing, test prompts and see usage. Also asked as: where is claude api console Inside the Console you will find a Workbench for trying prompts and model settings before writing code, a prompt generator and improver, usage and cost dashboards, rate-limit information for your tier, and organisation settings for inviting teammates and creating workspaces. It is separate from claude.ai, even though you can use the same email for both. If a link or tutorial points to an old address, start from Anthropic's documentation site and follow the link to the Console from there. What is the Claude API platform? The Claude Developer Platform is Anthropic's set of services for building with Claude: the API itself, the Console, SDKs, documentation and features such as tool use, batch processing, prompt caching, files and agent tooling. Also asked as: what is claude api platform Building blocks you will meet: Messages API: the core request for a model response. Tool use: let Claude call your functions and APIs. Message Batches: process large jobs asynchronously at lower cost. Prompt caching: reuse long, repeated context cheaply and quickly. Files API and PDF support: reuse uploaded documents. Agent SDK and MCP: build agents and connect tools in a standard way. Claude models are also available through cloud providers such as Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud Vertex AI, which suits teams already on those clouds. Where are the Claude API docs? Anthropic's developer documentation covers getting started, every API endpoint, the SDKs, model details, pricing, rate limits and guides on prompting, tool use, retrieval and agents. It is linked from anthropic.com and the Console. Also asked as: what are claude api docs Read these first: the quickstart, the Messages API reference, the models overview for current model names, the guide to tool use, and the prompt engineering guide. The docs include runnable examples in Python and TypeScript, and an API reference with every parameter. When a blog post or video disagrees with the docs, trust the docs; model names and parameters change, and older tutorials go stale quickly. What is the difference between Claude AI and the Claude API? Claude AI usually means claude.ai, the chat product for people, with a free tier and subscriptions. The Claude API is the developer interface for building Claude into your own software, paid per token used. The chat app gives you a ready interface, conversation history, projects, file uploads and apps on every device. The API gives you only the model: you send messages and get responses, and you build the interface, storage and logic yourself. Subscriptions and API credits are billed separately; a Pro plan does not cover API usage. Use claude.ai to learn, write and think; use the API when you want Claude inside a website, bot, app or automated workflow. How does the Claude API work? Your code sends an HTTPS request to the Messages endpoint with your API key, a model name, a maximum number of output tokens and a list of messages. Claude returns a response containing content blocks, a stop reason and token usage. Also asked as: how does claude api work Key ideas: Stateless: the API does not remember earlier calls; send the conversation history you want it to consider each time. System prompt: sets the role, rules and context for the whole conversation. Tokens: you pay for input and output tokens, and limits apply per minute. Streaming: receive the response as it is generated for a responsive UI. Tools: describe functions with JSON schemas; Claude replies with a tool call, you run it and send the result back. Errors come back with clear types, such as rate limits and temporary overload, which you handle with retries. How do I set up the Claude API? Install the SDK, set your key as an environment variable, and make a first request. In Python, that is three steps and about ten lines. Also asked as: how to set up claude api pip install anthropic export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=&quot;sk-ant-...&quot; # on Windows PowerShell: $env:ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=&quot;sk-ant-...&quot; from anthropic import Anthropic client = Anthropic() reply = client.messages.create( model=&quot;claude-sonnet-5-5&quot;, max_tokens=400, messages=[{&quot;role&quot;: &quot;user&quot;, &quot;content&quot;: &quot;Give me three RAG project ideas for students.&quot;}], ) print(reply.content[0].text) For projects, keep the key in a .env file loaded at startup and add .env to .gitignore. Check the models overview for the current model names. How do I use the Claude API in VS Code? The simplest route is Claude Code's VS Code extension, which brings Claude's coding agent into the editor. Alternatively, coding extensions that support multiple providers let you paste an Anthropic API key and choose a Claude model. Also asked as: vs code claude api With Claude Code, you install it, sign in with your Claude account or use an API key, and work with it in the editor: it reads your project, proposes edits shown as diffs and runs commands with your approval. Third-party extensions such as open-source coding assistants also accept Anthropic keys and bill usage to your API account. Whichever you use, set a spending limit in the Console, keep the key out of your settings files that get committed, and review every change before accepting it. Can the Claude API use skills? Yes. Agent Skills, packaged folders of instructions, scripts and resources that Claude loads when relevant, can be used through the Claude API together with its code execution tool, as well as in Claude Code and the Claude apps. Also asked as: can claude api use skills Anthropic provides some prebuilt skills, for example for working with document formats, and you can upload custom skills for your organisation, such as your report template or data-cleaning procedure. Claude sees a short description of each available skill and loads the full contents only when a task needs it, which keeps context small. Because this feature is newer and its request format may change, follow the current skills guide in the API documentation for the exact parameters, and test custom skills on small tasks first.

# What is the Claude app, the Claude SDK and API, and can Claude apply to jobs?
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/claude-app-sdk-api-guide/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-23

The Claude app is Anthropic's assistant on the web at claude.ai, on desktop for macOS and Windows, and on iOS and Android; Claude Code is its coding tool for the terminal and IDEs. Developers reach the same models through the Claude API, usually with Anthropic's official SDKs. This page covers the apps and where your data lives, the API and SDKs and how they differ, what the "overloaded" error means, how to connect Apify's scrapers to Claude, whether that is free, and whether Claude can apply to jobs for you. What is the Claude app? The Claude app is Anthropic's AI assistant, available in a browser at claude.ai and as desktop and mobile apps. You chat with it, upload files and images, create documents and small apps in a side panel, and connect it to tools. Also asked as: what is claude app All versions share one account, so conversations and projects appear everywhere you sign in. The desktop app adds conveniences such as a quick-launch shortcut and connecting local tools through the Model Context Protocol. The mobile app is good for voice and quick questions. Claude Code is a separate tool for developers that works directly on code in your terminal or IDE. The same family of Claude models powers all of them, with plans that set your usage limits. What are the Claude apps? The official Claude apps are the web app at claude.ai, desktop apps for macOS and Windows, mobile apps for iOS and Android, and Claude Code for the terminal and IDEs such as VS Code and JetBrains. All are published by Anthropic. Also asked as: what are claude apps Each suits a different job: Web and desktop: writing, research, analysing documents and spreadsheets, projects with shared files. Mobile: voice conversations, photos of notes or whiteboards, quick questions. Claude Code: reading a codebase, editing files, running tests and commands. Inside the chat apps, "artifacts" are small documents or apps Claude creates that you can preview, edit and share. Be careful with third-party apps that use the Claude name: unless the publisher is Anthropic or a known IDE vendor, avoid entering your credentials. Does the Claude app keep all data locally? No. The Claude apps store your conversations in your Anthropic account on Anthropic's servers, so they sync across devices. The desktop app is a client, not an offline model; nothing runs fully on your computer. Also asked as: does claude app keep all data locally What stays local depends on what you connect: files on your computer that you expose through a local MCP server are read on your machine and only the parts Claude uses are sent with the conversation. Anthropic's privacy settings let you control whether your chats may be used to improve models, and you can delete conversations. Check the privacy settings once and choose deliberately. If you need data to stay entirely on your own hardware, you need a local open-weight model, not Claude. What are the Claude APIs? The Claude API is Anthropic's HTTP interface for using Claude models in your own software. The core is the Messages API: you send a list of messages and settings, and get Claude's reply, with options for streaming, tool use, images, PDFs and structured outputs. Also asked as: what are claude apis Around it are supporting APIs: token counting, the Message Batches API for large asynchronous jobs at lower cost, a Files API for reusing uploaded documents, and features such as prompt caching to cut cost on repeated context. You authenticate with an API key from the Anthropic Console and pay per token used, separately from any chat subscription. The API is what you use to build a chatbot into a college project, add document Q&amp;A to an app, or run an agent on a server. What is the Claude SDK? The Claude SDKs are Anthropic's official client libraries for calling the API from code, available for Python, TypeScript and several other languages. There is also the Claude Agent SDK, for building agents on the same foundations as Claude Code. Also asked as: what is claude sdk A minimal Python example: from anthropic import Anthropic client = Anthropic() # reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from the environment msg = client.messages.create( model=&quot;claude-sonnet-5-5&quot;, max_tokens=500, messages=[{&quot;role&quot;: &quot;user&quot;, &quot;content&quot;: &quot;Explain BM25 in two sentences.&quot;}], ) print(msg.content[0].text) Install it with pip install anthropic. Check the model overview in the docs for the current model names, since new versions replace old ones regularly. What is the difference between the Claude API and SDK? The API is the service: HTTP endpoints that accept requests and return Claude's responses. An SDK is a library in your programming language that calls those endpoints for you, handling authentication, retries, streaming and typed responses. Also asked as: difference between claude api and sdk You can call the API directly with any HTTP client, which is useful for languages without an SDK or for quick tests with curl. In practice, the SDK saves effort and prevents mistakes: it retries temporary errors automatically, parses streaming events correctly, and gives editor autocompletion for parameters. Both reach the same models with the same limits and prices. Use the SDK for real projects and raw HTTP only when you have a reason. What does "Claude API is overloaded" mean? It means Anthropic's servers are temporarily under heavy load and could not process your request. The API returns an overloaded_error, with HTTP status 529, and the right response is to wait briefly and retry. Also asked as: what does claude api is overloaded mean It is not a problem with your key, code or account, and it is different from a rate-limit error, which means you exceeded your own limits. Handle it with retries using exponential backoff and a little randomness, so many clients do not retry at the same instant. The official SDKs already retry such errors a couple of times by default, and you can raise the retry count. In production, also add a fallback, such as a smaller model or a different provider, so users see a slower answer rather than an error. RAG.NextUpgrad uses multi-provider fallback for exactly this reason. How do I connect Apify to Claude? Apify provides an MCP server that exposes its scrapers, called Actors, as tools. Add the Apify MCP server to Claude, through the connectors settings or the desktop app's MCP configuration, with your Apify API token, and Claude can run Actors and read their results. Also asked as: how to connect apify to claude Once connected, you can ask Claude, for example, to collect the titles and links of recent posts from a public page using a suitable Actor, then summarise them. Keep three things in mind: scrape only public data you are allowed to collect and respect each site's terms; store your Apify token like a password; and limit which Actors are exposed so Claude cannot run expensive jobs by accident. Apify's documentation has current setup instructions for its MCP server. Is Apify for Claude free? Connecting Apify to Claude through its MCP server does not need a special paid add-on, but running Apify Actors uses your Apify account's platform usage. Apify has a free plan with a monthly usage allowance, and heavier use needs a paid plan. Also asked as: is claude apify free Your Claude plan applies on the Claude side as usual. Costs depend on the Actors you run, how many pages they process and how often; some Actors are maintained by third parties and have their own pricing. Start with small test runs and check usage in the Apify console before scheduling anything recurring. Apify's pricing page lists the current free allowance and plans. Can Claude apply to jobs for me? Claude can do most of the work around applying: tailoring your resume to each job description, drafting cover letters and referral messages, and preparing you for interviews. You should still submit applications yourself. Agent tools that control a browser can technically fill in forms, but automated applications on LinkedIn, Indeed and similar sites can break their terms of service and get accounts restricted. Mass-applying also produces poor matches that recruiters ignore. A better use of Claude: "Here is the job description and my resume. List the gaps, rewrite my project bullets using only facts from my resume, and draft a 100-word note to an engineer at the company." Then read, edit and send it yourself. Quality and a referral beat volume.

# How to use Claude Code for AI coding, and what Claude AI is
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/claude-code-ai-coding-guide/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-23

To code with Claude, install Claude Code, open a terminal in your project and run claude, then describe the change you want; it reads your files, edits them and runs commands with your approval. Claude itself is the family of AI models made by Anthropic, available on the web, desktop, mobile and through an API. This page covers how to start with Claude Code, what Claude is and how it is built, which version is free, which app to use, what Claude agents are, and how to vibe code without shipping a mess. How do I use Claude Code for AI coding? Install Claude Code, open a terminal in your project folder, run claude, and describe a task. It reads the codebase, proposes edits and terminal commands, and applies them when you approve. Also asked as: how to ai claude code A good first session: npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code cd my-project claude Then try "explain how this project is structured", followed by a small change such as "add input validation to the signup endpoint and a test for it". Claude Code also runs inside VS Code and JetBrains IDEs. Add a CLAUDE.md file at the project root with your build commands, coding style and rules; it is read at the start of every session. Work in small steps, review each diff and commit often so you can roll back. The official documentation lists the current installation options and the plans that include it. What is the Claude AI tool? Claude is an AI assistant from Anthropic. It writes, answers questions, analyses documents and images, and writes and debugs code, through a chat app, a coding tool and an API. Also asked as: what is claude ai tool · how claude ai works The same model family powers all of these surfaces. On claude.ai you chat, upload PDFs or spreadsheets and create documents or small apps in a side panel. Claude Code is the agentic coding tool for the terminal and IDEs. The Claude API lets developers build Claude into their own products with tool use, structured outputs and long context. Models come in tiers: Opus for the hardest work, Sonnet as the balanced default, and Haiku for fast, low-cost tasks. Students mostly use it for explaining concepts, reviewing code and drafting reports. How does Claude AI work? Claude is a large language model: a transformer neural network that predicts the next piece of text, one token at a time, based on everything earlier in the conversation. When you send a message, the text is split into tokens and processed together with the conversation history and any files you attached. The model generates a response token by token, and for harder problems it can reason through intermediate steps before answering. Tools extend it: it can search the web, run code or call your functions, and the results come back into its context. It does not look facts up by default and it has a training cutoff, so ask it to cite sources or use search for recent information. The attention mechanism from the 2017 Transformer paper is what lets it relate every part of a long input to every other part. How is Claude AI made? Claude is pretrained on a large body of text and code to predict the next token, then fine-tuned with human feedback and Anthropic's Constitutional AI method to be helpful, honest and harmless. Also asked as: how claude ai is made Pretraining gives the model knowledge and language ability. Fine-tuning shapes behaviour: people rate responses, and the model is trained towards the preferred ones. Constitutional AI, described in Anthropic's 2022 paper, adds a written set of principles; the model critiques and revises its own outputs against them, and that feedback is used for training, which reduces the need for humans to label harmful content. Anthropic also publishes safety research and runs evaluations before release. The training data and exact recipes are not public. When was Claude AI created? Anthropic was founded in 2021 by former OpenAI researchers, and the first Claude model was released to the public in March 2023. New generations have followed regularly since. Also asked as: when claude ai was created The Claude 3 family in March 2024 introduced the Haiku, Sonnet and Opus tiers that the product still uses. Claude Code arrived in early 2025 as a research preview and became generally available later that year. Each generation has improved coding, reasoning and context length, so advice written about an older model can be out of date. If a tutorial names a specific model version, check Anthropic's current model overview before copying its settings. Which Claude AI version is free? Claude has a free plan on claude.ai and in the apps, with a daily usage limit and access to a capable current model. Claude Code and the most capable models need a paid plan or API usage. The free plan is enough to learn: explaining code, debugging an error, reviewing a project report, or practising interview questions. Paid plans raise the limits, add the strongest models and include Claude Code. The API is billed by usage, separately from the chat plans, and is what you use to build Claude into your own app. Plans and limits change, so check the plans page on claude.ai for what is included today. For a college project, the free plan plus careful prompts goes a long way. Which Claude AI app is best? Use the app that matches the task: claude.ai or the desktop app for writing, research and analysis; Claude Code in the terminal or IDE for changing real code; the mobile app for quick questions and voice. The desktop app adds conveniences such as connecting local tools through the Model Context Protocol. Claude Code is the right choice once you want changes applied to files, tests run and commits made, rather than code pasted from a chat window. For a developer the usual setup is both: chat for thinking through a design, Claude Code for implementing it. Avoid unofficial third-party apps that ask for your login; use Anthropic's own apps or a known IDE integration. Where is the Claude AI website? Claude's chat website is claude.ai. Anthropic's company site, with model information, research and news, is anthropic.com, and the developer documentation is linked from there. Also asked as: where is claude ai website Sign in at claude.ai with an email or a Google account; the same account works in the desktop and mobile apps and in Claude Code. Developers create API keys in the Anthropic Console, which is separate from the chat subscription. Beware of look-alike domains and "Claude" apps from other publishers in app stores. The official mobile apps are published by Anthropic. What are Claude AI agents? Claude agents are systems where Claude works towards a goal in a loop: it decides the next step, calls tools such as search, code execution or your own APIs, reads the results and continues until the task is done. Claude Code is the best-known example: it reads files, runs commands and edits code on its own. Developers build their own agents with the Claude API's tool use, the Claude Agent SDK, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP), an open standard from Anthropic for connecting models to data sources and tools. A useful agent has a narrow job, a small set of well-described tools, limits on what it may do without asking, and logs you can review. Start with one tool and one task, measure it, then widen the scope. Can I vibe code with Claude? Yes. Vibe coding, describing what you want and letting the AI write the code while you steer by results, works well with Claude, especially in Claude Code or the artifacts panel on claude.ai. It is a great way to prototype a hackathon idea or a personal tool in an afternoon. The risks show up when the code has to last: duplicated logic, missing error handling, insecure defaults and secrets committed to the repository. Keep a few rules: ask for tests alongside features, read every diff before accepting it, commit after each working step, keep API keys in environment files, and ask Claude to review its own code for security issues. Judges and interviewers can tell when you cannot explain your own project, so make sure you understand what was written.

# What is Copilot CLI, and why is Copilot not showing in Outlook?
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/copilot-cli-and-outlook/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-23

Copilot CLI is GitHub Copilot's coding agent for the command line: you run it in a project folder, describe a task, and it reads code, edits files and runs commands with your approval. Separately, if Copilot is not showing in Outlook, the cause is nearly always the licence, the signed-in account, an outdated Outlook version or an admin policy. This page covers the CLI, how to fix Copilot missing from new and classic Outlook, what Copilot does in Outlook including scheduling, what Copilot skills are, and a short tutorial for Copilot's agents. What is Copilot CLI? GitHub Copilot CLI is a terminal application that brings GitHub Copilot's agent to the command line. It can explain a codebase, write and edit files, run shell commands and work with GitHub, asking for permission before it acts. You install it with npm and start it inside a repository: npm install -g @github/copilot cd my-project copilot Sign in with a GitHub account that has Copilot access, then type a request such as "find why the login test fails and fix it". It shows the commands and edits it wants to make, and you approve or reject each one. It can connect to extra tools through MCP servers. Treat it like any agent: small tasks, review the diff, run the tests, commit often. Does Copilot have a CLI? Yes. GitHub Copilot has a CLI, the Copilot CLI agent, and Copilot features are also available in terminals inside VS Code and other editors. Microsoft 365 Copilot does not have a general-purpose command line for end users. Also asked as: do copilot have cli Before the current Copilot CLI, GitHub offered an extension for the GitHub CLI, gh copilot, that suggested and explained shell commands. The newer Copilot CLI is a full agent that can change files and run multi-step tasks. If you prefer a terminal workflow, other coding agents work similarly: OpenAI's Codex CLI and Anthropic's Claude Code. All of them follow the same safety habits: run them in a project under version control, read every command before approving it, and never let them handle secrets. Why is Copilot not showing in Outlook? Usually because the account you are signed into does not have a Copilot licence, Outlook is out of date, or your organisation has not enabled Copilot. Personal Outlook.com accounts and work accounts also show Copilot differently. Also asked as: why copilot is not showing in outlook Check in this order: Licence: your work or school account needs Microsoft 365 Copilot for the full in-Outlook features; Copilot Chat may be all you have. Account: make sure Outlook is signed in with the licensed account, not a personal one. Version: update Outlook; new features reach current builds first. Admin policy: admins can turn Copilot features off or roll them out in stages. Restart: sign out of Office, sign in again and restart Outlook after a new licence is assigned. If colleagues with the same licence see it and you do not, ask IT to check your licence assignment. Why is Copilot not showing in classic Outlook? Classic Outlook for Windows shows Copilot only on recent versions of Microsoft 365 Apps. If you are on an older build or a slow update channel, Copilot features may be missing even with a valid licence. Also asked as: why is copilot not showing in outlook classic Go to File, then Office Account, then Update Options, and choose Update Now. Check which update channel you are on; organisations on a semi-annual channel get features months later than those on the current channel. Copilot features have generally appeared in the new Outlook and Outlook on the web first. If your organisation allows it, try the new Outlook toggle or Outlook on the web: if Copilot appears there, the problem is your classic Outlook build, not your licence. Why is the Copilot icon not showing in Outlook? If you have the licence and an up-to-date Outlook but no icon, the button is often hidden by the ribbon layout or not pinned. Copilot can also appear in different places depending on whether you are reading or writing an email. Also asked as: why is copilot icon not showing in outlook Try these: Switch between the simplified and classic ribbon, or use the "more options" menu on the ribbon, where overflow buttons hide. Look inside a message: summary options appear at the top of a thread, and drafting options appear in the compose window. In the new Outlook and on the web, check the app bar for the Copilot icon and pin it. Use "Customise ribbon" to add the Copilot button back if it was removed. If the icon still does not appear, the feature is probably not enabled for your account yet. How does Copilot work in Outlook? Copilot in Outlook uses a large language model to summarise email threads, draft replies and new emails from a short instruction, and coach you on tone and clarity. With a full licence it can also use context from your other work content. When you open a long thread, the summary gives the key points, decisions and open questions. To draft, type an instruction such as "politely decline, suggest next Tuesday instead" and adjust the length and tone. Coaching reviews your own draft for tone, reader sentiment and clarity. Copilot works within your permissions, so it only uses mail and files your account can already open. Read every draft before sending: it can state a date, figure or commitment that nobody agreed to. How does Copilot simplify scheduling in Outlook? Copilot can turn an email thread into a meeting: it suggests times based on attendees' availability, drafts the invitation with an agenda drawn from the thread, and saves you switching to the calendar. From a thread, use the scheduling option, review the proposed attendees and times, then edit the agenda Copilot drafted before sending. It can also help you prepare by summarising the related emails and files before the meeting. Availability depends on everyone's calendars being shared within your organisation, so external guests may still need a manual poll. Exact options vary by Outlook version and licence, and Microsoft adds scheduling features over time, so check what your version shows. Is there a tutorial for Copilot in Outlook? Yes. Microsoft's support and training pages have step-by-step guides, and the fastest way to learn is to use Copilot on your own inbox for a week with one feature a day. Also asked as: tutorial copilot outlook A practical sequence: Day 1: summarise your longest thread and check the summary against the emails. Day 2: draft a reply from a one-line instruction, then edit it into your own voice. Day 3: write a draft yourself and use coaching to improve it. Day 4: ask Copilot to find what a colleague asked you for last week. Day 5: schedule a meeting from a thread and review the agenda it proposes. Write instructions with the goal, the audience and the tone, for example "reply to my professor, formal, confirm the submission date". What are Copilot skills? Skills are packaged capabilities that an AI agent can load when a task needs them: instructions, examples and sometimes scripts for a specific job, such as running your project's tests or following your design system. GitHub Copilot's agents support them. A skill usually lives as a folder with a short description file that says what it does and when to use it, plus any supporting files. The agent reads only the descriptions up front and loads a skill's full contents when a request matches, which keeps the context small and focused. That is different from tools, which are functions the agent can call, and from MCP servers, which connect it to outside systems. Good skills are narrow, clearly described and tested, like good functions. In Microsoft 365, "skills" is also used loosely for the actions an agent built in Copilot Studio can perform. Is there a tutorial for the Copilot agent? Yes. The quickest start is agent mode in VS Code: open Copilot Chat, switch to agent mode, and give it a small, testable task. On GitHub, you can also assign an issue to Copilot and review the pull request it opens. Also asked as: tutorial copilot agent A first session in VS Code: Open a repository with tests and start Copilot Chat in agent mode. Add a .github/copilot-instructions.md file with build commands and coding rules. Ask: "Add input validation to the signup endpoint, write tests, run them and fix failures." Review each edit and terminal command before approving. Read the final diff and run the tests yourself. For the GitHub coding agent, write the issue like a ticket for a new teammate: goal, files involved, acceptance criteria. Then review its pull request as carefully as any human's.

# Will Copilot share my data? Where Copilot data goes, and connectors
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/copilot-data-privacy/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-23

Whether Copilot shares your data depends on which Copilot you use. Microsoft 365 Copilot for work and school keeps your prompts and responses inside your organisation's Microsoft 365 environment, respects existing permissions, and does not use them to train the foundation models. Consumer Copilot for personal accounts and GitHub Copilot have their own privacy settings. This page explains the Copilot app, what is saved and where, whether OpenAI sees your data, how GitHub Copilot handles code, what connectors are, and which Copilot fits which job, with agent examples. What is the Copilot app? There are two main Copilot apps. The Microsoft 365 Copilot app, formerly the Microsoft 365 or Office app, is the hub for work files, Copilot Chat and agents. The Microsoft Copilot app is the consumer assistant for personal accounts on Windows, the web and phones. Also asked as: what is copilot app The Microsoft 365 Copilot app opens your recent Word, Excel and PowerPoint files, gives you Copilot Chat grounded in the web and, with a licence, in your work data, and lists agents your organisation provides. The consumer Copilot app is a general assistant like ChatGPT: chat, voice, image generation and web answers. GitHub Copilot, by contrast, lives inside code editors, not in a standalone app. If you are unsure which you have, check the account shown in the corner: a work account means the Microsoft 365 version. Will Copilot share my data? Microsoft 365 Copilot does not share your work data outside your organisation's tenant, and only shows you content you already have permission to open. Consumer Copilot processes your data under Microsoft's privacy statement, with settings that control some uses. For work accounts, Microsoft's commitments include: prompts, responses and data accessed through Microsoft Graph are not used to train the foundation models; data stays within the Microsoft 365 service boundary; and existing security, compliance and data residency commitments apply. For personal accounts, review Copilot's privacy settings, which include controls over personalisation and whether your conversations may be used to improve models. In both cases, do not paste passwords, identity numbers or other people's private data into a prompt. Does Copilot save your data? Yes, in most cases. Consumer Copilot keeps your conversation history until you delete it. Microsoft 365 Copilot stores interactions within your organisation's environment so they can be governed by retention and compliance policies. On a personal account, you can delete individual conversations or your whole history from Copilot's settings or your Microsoft privacy dashboard. On a work account, your organisation decides how long Copilot interactions are kept, in the same way it decides for email and Teams chats, and deleting a chat from your view may not delete the organisation's record. Files you upload to Copilot Chat on a work account are typically stored in your OneDrive. Assume what you type into any assistant may be kept and reviewed. Where is Copilot data stored? Microsoft 365 Copilot data is stored in Microsoft's cloud within your organisation's Microsoft 365 tenant, under the same data residency commitments as the rest of your Microsoft 365 data. Consumer Copilot data is stored in Microsoft's cloud under its consumer privacy terms. Also asked as: where copilot data is stored For organisations, that means Copilot interaction data sits with your mailbox and other Microsoft 365 content, and is covered by tools such as retention policies, audit logs and eDiscovery. Organisations in the EU also have Microsoft's EU Data Boundary commitments. Generated files and uploads usually land in OneDrive or SharePoint, inside the same tenant. If your college or company has specific data residency needs, the Microsoft Learn page on Copilot privacy and the admin centre are the authoritative sources. Does Copilot share data with OpenAI? Microsoft states that Microsoft 365 Copilot uses OpenAI models hosted in Microsoft's Azure cloud, not OpenAI's own services, so your prompts and work data are not sent to OpenAI and are not used to train OpenAI's models. The distinction is between the model and the service. OpenAI builds the GPT models; Microsoft runs copies of them in its own data centres through the Azure OpenAI Service and its Copilot infrastructure. OpenAI does not receive the data flowing through Microsoft's deployment. The same separation applies to the consumer Copilot app, which runs on Microsoft's infrastructure under Microsoft's privacy statement. Microsoft has also added models from other providers in some features, and its documentation notes where data handling differs, so check those notes if your organisation enables them. Does GitHub Copilot share your data? GitHub Copilot sends the code context around your cursor and your chat prompts to GitHub's service to generate suggestions. For business and enterprise plans, GitHub states that this data is not used to train its models. Individual plans have settings controlling such use. On Copilot Business and Enterprise, organisation admins control policies such as which models are allowed and whether suggestions matching public code are blocked. On individual plans, check your GitHub Copilot settings for options about data use for product improvement and choose deliberately. Practical rules for any plan: keep secrets out of source files and prompts, add sensitive files to content exclusions where available, and follow your employer's policy on AI tools. The details per plan are in GitHub's Copilot documentation and trust centre. What are Copilot connectors? Copilot connectors, previously called Microsoft Graph connectors, bring content from systems outside Microsoft 365, such as ServiceNow, Jira, Confluence, Salesforce, file shares or websites, into the index that Microsoft 365 Copilot searches. Without connectors, Copilot only knows your Microsoft 365 content: mail, Teams, SharePoint and OneDrive. With a connector, an employee can ask "what is the status of the onboarding tickets for the new interns?" and get an answer that draws on items in the ticketing system, with links back to them. Microsoft provides prebuilt connectors for many popular services, and developers can build custom ones for internal databases. Admins set them up, so as a user you will see their results appear in Copilot answers and Microsoft Search. How do Copilot connectors work? A connector crawls an external system, converts its items into a standard schema with their text, properties and access permissions, and loads them into the Microsoft Graph index. Copilot then retrieves from that index at question time. The important detail is access control: each item carries an access list, so a user only sees results for items they could open in the original system. Connectors refresh on a schedule, with full crawls and faster incremental crawls, so recent changes appear after a short delay. This is retrieval-augmented generation at company scale: the same pattern I built in RAG.NextUpgrad, where retrieval quality decides answer quality. Clean titles, good metadata and correct permissions in the source system make connectors far more useful. Which Copilot is right for me? Pick by the work you do. Microsoft 365 Copilot for documents, email and meetings at work, consumer Copilot for personal questions and creativity, GitHub Copilot for writing code, and Copilot Studio for building your own agents. A quick guide: Student or personal use: the free consumer Copilot, or Copilot Chat through your college account. Office worker: Microsoft 365 Copilot if your organisation licenses it; Copilot Chat otherwise. Developer: GitHub Copilot in your editor and on GitHub. Team that needs a custom assistant: Copilot Studio or Agent Builder. Microsoft Learn publishes a comparison of the Copilot offerings that is kept up to date; use it to check current features before buying anything. What are some examples of Copilot agents? Copilot agents include Microsoft's built-in research and data analysis agents in Microsoft 365 Copilot, meeting and project agents in Teams, GitHub Copilot's coding agent, and custom agents organisations build with Copilot Studio. Also asked as: examples copilot agents Examples of custom agents that work well: An HR policy agent that answers leave and travel questions from the policy documents, with citations. An IT helpdesk agent that answers common questions and creates a ticket when it cannot. A sales assistant that summarises an account from CRM records through a connector. A college admissions agent that answers questions from the prospectus and fee notices. A coding agent that picks up small GitHub issues and opens pull requests for review. The best agents have a narrow job, trusted knowledge sources, a clear handover to a person, and logs you review every week.

# Copilot vs Claude and Gemini vs Claude: the differences and when to use each
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/copilot-gemini-vs-claude/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-23

Copilot is Microsoft's AI assistant, built into Windows, Edge and Microsoft 365, running mostly on OpenAI models and, in some features, Anthropic's Claude. Claude is Anthropic's assistant and model family, used through claude.ai, Claude Code and an API. Gemini is Google's assistant and model family. All three are capable; they differ mainly in integration, strengths and limits. This page explains how Copilot and Claude relate, when to use each, how Claude compares with GitHub Copilot for coding, how Gemini and Claude differ, and how ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini compare in 2026. What are Copilot and Claude? Copilot is Microsoft's brand of AI assistants: the consumer Copilot app, Microsoft 365 Copilot for work, and GitHub Copilot for code. Claude is a family of AI models made by Anthropic, available in the Claude apps, in Claude Code for software development, and through the Claude API. Copilot is defined by where it lives: inside Word, Excel, Outlook, Teams, Windows and code editors, with access to your work context. Claude is defined by the models: strong at reasoning, long documents, writing and coding, with its own apps and tools. Both are used by students and companies, often side by side. Your choice depends on whether you want an assistant inside the tools you already use, or a strong standalone assistant and coding agent. Are Copilot and Claude the same? No. They are different products from different companies: Copilot from Microsoft, Claude from Anthropic. They do overlap, because Microsoft has added Claude models as options in parts of Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Studio, and GitHub Copilot lets you choose Claude models. So "using Claude in Copilot" is possible in some places: for example, picking a Claude model in GitHub Copilot's model picker or in certain Microsoft 365 Copilot features where your organisation enables it. In those cases, Microsoft's product, permissions and data handling apply, with a Claude model doing the generation. Using Claude directly through claude.ai or Claude Code gives you Anthropic's own features, such as Projects, artifacts and Claude Code's agent tooling. What is the difference between Copilot and Claude? The biggest difference is integration versus depth. Copilot is woven into Microsoft's apps and sees your work context; Claude is a standalone assistant and API known for long-context understanding, careful writing and strong coding. Practical differences: Context: Microsoft 365 Copilot can search your organisation's mail, files and meetings; Claude works from what you give it or connect through integrations. Coding: GitHub Copilot plugs into editors; Claude Code is an agent that works across your repository from the terminal or IDE. Documents: Claude handles very long documents in one go; Copilot is strongest on documents already in Microsoft 365. Data: each follows its own company's privacy terms and enterprise controls. Many people use Copilot at work and Claude for deep reading, writing and coding. When should I use Copilot vs Claude? Use Copilot when your task involves Microsoft 365 content, such as summarising a Teams meeting, drafting from your Outlook mail or analysing an Excel sheet, or when your organisation requires it. Use Claude for long documents, careful writing, complex reasoning and serious coding work. Also asked as: when to use copilot vs claude Examples: "What did the client ask for in last week's meetings?": Copilot. "Turn this Word report into slides": Copilot in PowerPoint. "Read these three long PDFs and compare their methods": Claude. "Refactor this module and fix the failing tests": Claude Code, or GitHub Copilot's agent. "Help me write my project report clearly": either; Claude is often preferred for prose. For company data, use the tool your organisation approves. How does Claude compare to Copilot for coding? GitHub Copilot is an assistant built into editors and GitHub, with completions, chat, agent mode and a coding agent for issues, and a choice of models including Claude. Claude Code is Anthropic's agentic coding tool that reads your repository, edits files and runs commands from the terminal or IDE. Also asked as: how does claude ai compare to copilot Choose GitHub Copilot if your team lives on GitHub, wants inline completions in VS Code, Visual Studio or JetBrains, and needs enterprise policies. Choose Claude Code for long, multi-step changes across a codebase, where its agent loop and project memory file shine. Many developers use both: Copilot completions while typing, Claude Code for larger tasks. The fair test is one real task in your own repository with each, judged on how much you had to fix. Gemini vs Claude: which is better? Neither is better at everything. Gemini is strong at multimodal input, including video and long audio, very long context and integration with Google's apps; Claude is strong at careful writing, following detailed instructions, long documents and coding. For students: Gemini fits naturally if you use Google Docs, Gmail, YouTube lectures and Android, and Google has run free plan offers for students. Claude is excellent for reading and writing long reports, explaining code, and agentic coding with Claude Code. Both have free tiers. Run the same three tasks in both, such as summarising a paper, explaining a bug and drafting an email, and keep the one that needs less fixing. What is the difference between Gemini and Claude? Gemini is made by Google and built into Google Search, Workspace and Android; Claude is made by Anthropic and offered through its own apps, Claude Code and its API, as well as through cloud platforms. The models differ in strengths and in how each company approaches safety and features. Notable differences: Media: Gemini natively handles video and audio input and generates images and video; Claude works with text, images and documents. Ecosystem: Gemini connects to Gmail, Drive, Maps and YouTube; Claude connects through integrations and MCP. Coding tools: Google has Gemini CLI and Antigravity; Anthropic has Claude Code. Safety approach: Anthropic is known for its Constitutional AI training and safety research; Google DeepMind has its own frameworks. Both offer free and paid plans and developer APIs. When should I use Gemini vs Claude? Use Gemini when your work involves Google Workspace, YouTube videos, audio or video files, or you want image and video generation. Use Claude for long documents, structured writing, detailed analysis and coding with Claude Code. Also asked as: when to use gemini vs claude A simple split many developers use: Summarise a YouTube lecture or analyse a video: Gemini. Draft inside Google Docs or Gmail: Gemini. Compare long PDFs or write a detailed report: Claude. Make multi-file code changes with tests: Claude Code. Quick everyday questions: whichever you have open. For an app you are building, test both APIs on your own data, and design your code so switching models is a configuration change, as I did with multi-provider fallback in RAG.NextUpgrad. How does Gemini compare to Claude for long documents? Both handle long documents well. Gemini offers very large context windows and handles mixed media, such as a PDF with images, or a long recording; Claude is known for careful reading, accurate quoting and following detailed instructions across long inputs. Practical tips for either: ask for answers with page or section references so you can check them; ask specific questions rather than "summarise everything"; and for very large collections, use retrieval, such as NotebookLM for Gemini or Projects in Claude, instead of pasting everything at once. Long-context models can still miss details in the middle of huge inputs, so verify anything important against the source. ChatGPT vs Claude vs Gemini in 2026: which is best? In 2026 the three are close in overall quality, and each new model release shifts the lead on specific tasks. The best choice depends on your tasks, your tools and which one gives you better answers in your own tests. Also asked as: 2026 chatgpt vs claude vs gemini A practical summary: ChatGPT is the broad all-rounder with a large ecosystem; Claude is strong for writing, long documents and coding agents; Gemini is strong for multimodal work and Google integration. Free tiers of all three are enough for most students. Rather than trusting rankings, spend twenty minutes running five of your real tasks in each. Many people end up using two: one for daily work and one for coding or deep analysis.

# Copilot Notebooks and Copilot premium requests, explained
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/copilot-notebooks-premium-requests/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-23

Copilot Notebooks are workspaces in Microsoft 365 Copilot where you gather the files, pages, meeting notes and links for one project, so Copilot answers questions and drafts content using that collection as its main source. They are also arriving in OneNote. "Copilot premium" is a looser phrase: it can mean Microsoft's higher consumer plans with more Copilot capability, or the premium requests that GitHub Copilot counts when you use its most capable models. This page explains notebooks, when to use them, and what premium plans and premium requests include, cost you in usage, and when they reset. What are Copilot Notebooks? Copilot Notebooks are project spaces in Microsoft 365 Copilot. You add references, such as Word files, PDFs, Copilot Pages, meeting notes and links, and Copilot uses that set as context for every question and draft in the notebook. Think of a notebook as a focused folder with a built-in assistant. Instead of searching all your mail and files, Copilot prioritises the material you chose, which makes answers more relevant and easier to check. Notebooks keep your Copilot responses and notes together, so you can come back to a project days later without rebuilding the context. They are similar in spirit to Google's NotebookLM, but they live inside Microsoft 365 and follow your organisation's permissions and compliance settings. How do Copilot Notebooks work? You create a notebook, add references, then chat with Copilot inside it. Copilot retrieves relevant passages from those references, answers with citations to them, and can save useful responses as pages in the notebook. Under the hood this is retrieval-augmented generation scoped to a chosen set of documents, the same principle I used in the OCR &amp; Speech Workspace, where chat is limited to one document and answers cite page numbers. Scoping improves accuracy because Copilot has fewer irrelevant files to confuse it. References stay where they are stored, in OneDrive or SharePoint, and permissions still apply, so sharing a notebook does not give others access to files they could not already open. Keep references current: if you update a file, check that the notebook points to the right version. When should I use Copilot Notebooks? Use a notebook when you work on the same body of material over days or weeks and keep asking questions about it: a course module, a research project, a client engagement, a product launch or exam revision. Also asked as: when to use copilot notebooks Good fits: A semester course: lecture slides, notes and past papers in one notebook for revision questions. A thesis or report: sources, drafts and supervisor feedback together. A client project: proposal, meeting notes and requirements, so drafts stay consistent. Interview preparation: job description, company documents and your notes. For a one-off question, plain Copilot Chat is quicker. For anything where you need answers from exactly your chosen files, and to see where each answer came from, a notebook is the better tool. What are Copilot Notebooks in OneNote? Microsoft has been bringing Copilot Notebooks into OneNote, so the AI project space sits alongside your handwritten and typed notes. You can gather pages and files for a topic and ask Copilot questions grounded in them. This suits students who already keep class notes in OneNote: your notes become part of the material Copilot can use when you ask for a summary, a list of key definitions or practice questions. It also keeps the familiar OneNote structure of sections and pages. Availability depends on your Microsoft 365 plan, licence and OneNote version, and features roll out in stages, so update OneNote and check whether the Copilot notebook option appears for your account. How do Copilot Notebooks work in OneNote? In OneNote, you create or open a Copilot notebook, add the pages and files you want it to use, and ask Copilot questions in the Copilot pane. Answers draw on that material and point back to the pages they used. A practical study workflow: create a notebook for one subject, add your lecture notes and the syllabus, then ask for a one-page summary per unit, a list of terms with definitions, and ten practice questions. Check every answer against your notes, because summaries can drop a condition or merge two ideas. Use Copilot to find gaps, for example "which topics in the syllabus have no notes yet?". Keep personal or sensitive notes out of shared notebooks, since anyone with access can query them. What is Copilot premium? "Copilot premium" has no single meaning. For Microsoft's consumer Copilot, it refers to the paid plans that include more Copilot capability across apps. For GitHub Copilot, it usually refers to premium requests, the metered allowance for the most capable models and features. On the Microsoft side, the free Copilot app covers everyday chat, while paid Microsoft 365 consumer plans add Copilot inside Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook with higher limits; Microsoft has renamed and restructured these plans more than once. On the GitHub side, every paid Copilot plan includes a monthly number of premium requests, and you can pay for more. Before buying anything, confirm which product the page you are reading is about, because the names overlap. What does Copilot premium include? On Microsoft's paid consumer plans, it typically includes Copilot in the Microsoft 365 desktop and web apps, higher usage limits, priority access to newer features and image creation. On GitHub, premium requests unlock the most capable models, agent mode and the coding agent at higher volumes. Because both sides change often, rely on the current plan pages rather than lists in older articles. A sensible check before paying: list the three tasks you would use it for each week, try them on the free tier first, and see whether limits or missing features actually block you. Students often find that the free consumer Copilot, Copilot Chat through a college account, and GitHub Copilot's free tier or student benefits cover most needs. What is the difference between Copilot basic and premium? The basic, free tiers give general chat and limited use of advanced features. Premium tiers add Copilot inside the Office apps or more powerful coding features, higher limits and earlier access to new models and tools. In GitHub Copilot, the practical difference is which models and features you can use and how often: base models are included for routine completions and chat, while premium models and agent features draw on the premium request allowance. In Microsoft's consumer Copilot, the difference is mainly whether Copilot works inside Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook and how much you can use it. Neither tier changes the need to check outputs; premium means more capability and volume, not guaranteed accuracy. What are Copilot premium requests? Premium requests are GitHub Copilot's unit for metering use of its more capable models and features. Each chat message, agent step or coding agent session that uses a premium model consumes one or more requests from your monthly allowance. Models have multipliers: a lightweight model may count as a fraction of a request or be free on paid plans, while the most capable models count as several requests per message. Your plan includes a monthly allowance, and organisations can set a budget for paid overage. You can see your usage in your GitHub settings, and in the editor the model picker shows which models are premium. To stretch the allowance, use an included model for routine edits and save premium models for hard debugging and design. When do Copilot premium requests reset? GitHub Copilot's premium request allowance resets at the start of each monthly billing cycle; GitHub's documentation states the exact reset time. Unused requests do not roll over. If you run out before the reset, Copilot falls back to included models, or you can enable paid overage if your plan or organisation allows it. Check the usage page in your GitHub settings to see how many you have used and when the counter resets. For organisations, admins can view usage per user and set spending limits. Because GitHub has adjusted allowances and multipliers since premium requests were introduced, check the current billing documentation instead of numbers quoted in forums.

# Copilot vs Copilot Pro, Copilot+ laptops, and can Copilot make videos?
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/copilot-pro-laptops-and-video/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-23

Free Microsoft Copilot gives you chat, web answers with citations, voice and image creation. Microsoft's paid consumer plans, which started as Copilot Pro and have since been folded into Microsoft 365 consumer subscriptions, add Copilot inside Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook, higher limits and earlier access to new features. Copilot does not edit videos itself, though Microsoft offers AI video tools elsewhere. On laptops, "Copilot" means the Copilot key and app, and Copilot+ PCs are Windows laptops with a fast neural processing unit for on-device AI. This page covers each point and how to choose a laptop. Copilot vs Copilot Pro: what is the difference? Free Copilot is the general assistant on the web, in Windows and on phones. Copilot Pro was Microsoft's paid consumer upgrade, adding Copilot in the Microsoft 365 apps, priority access at busy times and higher limits; Microsoft has since moved these benefits into its Microsoft 365 consumer plans. In practice, the free version is enough for questions, writing help, summaries and images. The paid tier matters if you want Copilot working inside your Word documents, Excel sheets, PowerPoint decks and Outlook mail with a personal account, or you hit usage limits often. Work and school accounts are different again: they use Microsoft 365 Copilot or Copilot Chat under the organisation's licence. Because Microsoft renames and rebundles consumer plans, check the current plan comparison before buying. Which Copilot Pro features are free? Many former Pro-only features are now in free Copilot: access to strong models, web-grounded answers, voice conversations, image creation within limits, and vision features that understand images you share. What generally remains paid on consumer plans is Copilot inside the Microsoft 365 desktop and web apps with a personal account, higher usage limits for heavy features, and early access to experiments. Free use also has daily limits on things like image creation and the most advanced modes. If you are a student with a college Microsoft 365 account, check whether your institution provides Copilot Chat or Microsoft 365 Copilot, which may give you more than any consumer plan. Microsoft's plan pages list the current split. Is there a tutorial for Copilot Pro? Yes. Microsoft's support pages have guides for Copilot in each Microsoft 365 app, and the quickest way to learn is to try one task a day in the app you already use. Also asked as: tutorial copilot pro A five-day plan: Word: turn rough notes into a structured report, then ask for a shorter version for a different reader. PowerPoint: create a draft deck from that Word file and fix the design yourself. Excel: format a dataset as a table and ask three specific questions about it. Outlook: summarise a long thread and draft a reply from a one-line instruction. Copilot app: plan a week of study with deadlines, then ask it to make a checklist. Write prompts with the goal, the audience, the source material and the format you want. Does Copilot make videos? Not in the chat itself. Copilot creates text and images, but it does not edit or render videos. Microsoft offers AI video generation separately, and its Clipchamp editor is where you assemble a finished video. Also asked as: does copilot do videos Copilot is still useful for video work: it can write a script, a shot list, captions and a title and description, and generate images for scenes or thumbnails. You then record and edit in Clipchamp, which is built into Windows, or another editor. For explainer videos, a script from Copilot plus your own voice-over and screen recording usually beats generated footage. Check what is current, because Microsoft has been adding video features to its creative tools. Can Copilot create AI videos? Microsoft has offered AI video generation through separate tools rather than the main Copilot chat, including a video creator in the Bing mobile app built on OpenAI's Sora model. Availability depends on region and the tool's current status. Generated clips are short and best used as B-roll or illustrations, not as a full video. Write a specific prompt: subject, setting, camera movement, lighting and style, for example "slow aerial shot over green rice fields at sunrise, cinematic". Generate several versions and pick the best. Then edit the clips together with narration and text in Clipchamp. Label AI-generated footage when you publish it, and never generate videos of real people without their consent. Can Copilot make videos from photos? Not directly in Copilot chat. To turn photos into a video, use Clipchamp or the Photos app's video tools on Windows, which assemble images with transitions, music and text, or ask Copilot to write an ffmpeg command that builds a slideshow. In Clipchamp, import your photos, drag them onto the timeline, set how long each shows, add transitions, music and captions, then export. If you want the photos to move, for example a slow zoom or pan, use Clipchamp's motion effects. For command-line users, ask Copilot "write an ffmpeg command that turns img001.jpg to img030.jpg into a video showing each image for three seconds", run it, and check the result. Image-to-video AI models can animate a single photo, but they live in separate tools. Can Copilot watch or work with videos? Copilot in Microsoft Edge can summarise and answer questions about some online videos, typically by using their transcripts. It does not reliably analyse the visual content of every frame of a long video. For YouTube videos with captions, open the video in Edge, open Copilot in the sidebar and ask for a summary or key points with timestamps. For your own recordings, generate a transcript first, for example with Word's Transcribe or Teams for meetings, then give the transcript to Copilot. For visual questions, take screenshots of the moments that matter and share those as images. Copilot cannot record video for you; for screen recordings use the Windows Snipping Tool or Clipchamp. What is Copilot in a laptop? On a Windows laptop, Copilot is the built-in AI assistant you open from the taskbar or the Copilot key on newer keyboards. On Copilot+ PCs, extra AI features run on the laptop's own neural processing unit instead of the cloud. Also asked as: what is copilot in laptop Every recent Windows 11 laptop can run the Copilot app, which uses Microsoft's cloud models. Copilot+ PCs add on-device features, such as improved Windows Studio camera effects, live captions with translation, image tools in Photos and Paint, and search that understands natural language, with availability varying by region. The Copilot key simply launches the assistant. If you mainly use Copilot for chat and writing, any decent Windows laptop works; the Copilot+ label matters for the on-device features. What is the best Copilot+ laptop? The best Copilot+ laptop is the one that fits your work, budget and comfort. Copilot+ models come from Microsoft Surface, Dell, HP, Lenovo, ASUS, Acer and Samsung, with Qualcomm Snapdragon X, Intel Core Ultra or AMD Ryzen AI processors. Also asked as: best copilot plus laptop · best copilot ai laptop Choose by use: Long battery life and light weight: Snapdragon-based models are strong, but check that the apps you need run well on Arm. Development and compatibility: Intel or AMD models run every Windows app natively, including older tools. Light gaming or GPU work: look for models with a discrete graphics card. Read reviews that test battery life, heat and keyboard quality, and try the keyboard and screen in a shop if you can. What should I look for in a Copilot AI laptop? Look for a Copilot+ certified processor with a capable neural processing unit, at least 16 GB of RAM, a fast SSD of 512 GB or more if you code or edit media, a good screen and long battery life. Microsoft's Copilot+ PC requirements include an NPU of at least 40 trillion operations per second, 16 GB of RAM and 256 GB of storage, so certified laptops meet a baseline. For students in computer science, 16 GB is the practical minimum and 32 GB is comfortable for Docker, virtual machines and local AI models. The NPU helps Windows AI features but does not replace a GPU for training models; for serious machine learning work, use cloud GPUs or Google Colab. Check ports, warranty and service centres near you before buying.
