# Free AI tools every CS student should learn in 2026: coding assistants, models, notebooks, deployment and the ones I built, with no signup
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/free-ai-tools-for-students/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-09-24

## Which AI tools should a CS student learn first?

**Five categories, in this order: a coding assistant in your editor, so you build faster; a way to call a model, a free API tier or a local runner; a notebook with a free GPU, for experiments and fine-tuning; a database with a free tier, so projects have real persistence; and a platform to deploy on, so projects have a URL. Everything else is optional until a project demands it. Learn each by shipping something with it, not by watching a tutorial about it.**


I mentor 200-plus students through TechVerse Enclave and the same question arrives weekly: which tools? The list below is what I actually use and what students who finish projects actually use, with the free-tier limits that matter. Because signup friction stops more students than difficulty does, I also built fifteen tools that need no account at all, at tools.scult.in [15].

> A tool you have to sign up for is a tool you try tomorrow. A tool that opens in a tab is a tool you use now. That is the whole reason tools.scult.in exists.
> <cite>Pranjul Rathour</cite>

## Which coding assistant should students use?

**One you can afford and that lives in your editor. GitHub Copilot is free for verified students through the Student Developer Pack and works inside VS Code [5][6]. Cursor is an AI-first editor with a free tier [13]. Claude Code runs an agent in your terminal that can read, edit and run your project [14]. Pick one, learn its limits, and use it for boilerplate, tests, refactors and explanations of unfamiliar code. Turn it off when you are learning a fundamental for the first time, or you will not learn it.**



The rule I give mentees: assistants make you faster at what you understand and slower at learning what you do not. Write your first RAG pipeline by hand; use the assistant for the tenth.

## How do students get free access to LLMs?

**Three ways. Free API tiers: Google AI Studio gives Gemini API access with a free quota [10]; Groq offers fast inference on open models with a free tier [11]; OpenRouter routes to many models, some free [12]. Local models: Ollama runs open-weight models on your laptop with no account and no cost [4]. Hosted playgrounds: Hugging Face hosts thousands of models and free courses [3]. Start with a free API for speed, and Ollama for privacy and unlimited experimentation.**



Free tiers change often; the pricing pages are the truth and this table is a map [10][11][12].

## Where can students get free GPUs?

**Google Colab gives free GPU sessions with time and availability limits, enough for QLoRA on a small model [1]. Kaggle Notebooks give weekly GPU hours with a generous quota, and host datasets you can use directly [2]. Hugging Face Spaces can run demos with optional paid GPU [3]. For learning: fine-tune a 1 to 3B model on Colab, then move to Kaggle when you need longer runs. Save checkpoints to Drive or the Hub because sessions end.**


## Which databases and backends have free tiers good enough for projects?

**Supabase gives hosted Postgres with auth, storage and the pgvector extension on a free tier, which is a complete backend for a RAG project [7]. Firebase and MongoDB Atlas have free tiers too. For deploying a Python API, Railway and Render both offer free or trial tiers that sleep when idle [8][9]. GitHub Pages hosts static front ends for free, including this site. The pattern: one Postgres, one API host, one static host, all free until you have users.**




## What free tools did you build, and why no signup?

**Fifteen browser tools at tools.scult.in, a 1,211-prompt library where every prompt is stamped with the model and date it was tested against, a 50,000-plus agent-skills library, and a public MCP server so agents can call the same tools [15]. Thirteen of the fifteen tools never send a byte to a server; they run entirely in your browser, which is both faster and the simplest privacy story there is [17]. No signup because every signup screen is a place where a student decides to do it later.**



Every calculator shows its formula so you can check it rather than trust it, and the prompt library's stamps exist because a prompt that worked on one model version is a hypothesis on the next.

## How should students use AI tools without hurting their learning?

**Decide before each task whether the goal is output or understanding. For output, a deadline, a boilerplate, a refactor, use the assistant fully and review what it wrote. For understanding, a new algorithm, a first pipeline, a concept for an exam, write it yourself first, then ask the assistant to critique it. Never submit code you cannot explain line by line, because the interview will ask you to. The students who do best treat assistants like a senior colleague: consult often, copy never without reading.**



## Which AI tools help with research, writing and productivity?

**For reading papers: a chat model with the PDF, asking for the method and the limitations, then reading the paper anyway. For writing: an assistant for structure and clarity, never for facts you have not checked. For notes: any tool that exports plain text, so your notes outlive the tool. For search: AI answer engines for orientation, primary sources for anything you will cite. The habit that matters is checking the source, which no tool does for you.**


## What free AI tools are there for design and content?

**For diagrams and slides, most design tools now have free AI features; for images, be careful with licences and never present generated images as photographs of real events. For content, the same rule as writing: structure from the model, facts from sources. The colour palette generator and favicon generator at tools.scult.in cover the two design tasks every student project actually needs, with contrast checks built in [15].**



## Which tools will still matter in five years?

**None of the specific ones, probably, and all of the skills: prompting a model precisely, evaluating its output, deploying a service, reading documentation, reading a paper, and knowing when to switch the assistant off. Learn tools as instances of those skills, and the next tool is an afternoon, not a semester. My longer list with the reasoning is on the portfolio [16].**




## Where should I start today?

**Open tools.scult.in, use one tool, copy one stamped prompt into your assistant, and ship one page to GitHub Pages before you sleep.** For a hands-on session at your college that ends with every student having a deployed project built with free tools, email pranjulrathour41@gmail.com or use pranjulrathour.scult.in/invite.

# From a BCA in India to GenAI engineer: how I got here, what actually mattered, and what I would tell my first-year self
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/from-bca-student-to-genai-engineer/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-09-24

## Can you become a GenAI engineer from a BCA at a college nobody has heard of?

**Yes. I did a Bachelor of Computer Applications at Dr. Virendra Swarup Institute of Computer Studies, 2023 to 2026, and by the first half of 2026 I had shipped five production AI systems as a GenAI engineer and was leading engineering for a 14-member team at SCULT INDIA. Not one interview that mattered asked about the college. Every one asked about what I had built and what broke. This page is the path, without the parts that make it sound inevitable.**


The full resume with dates is on the portfolio [1]. What follows is the version with the decisions in it.

> The certificate says BCA. The GitHub says five production AI apps, three first prizes, a 14-member team. Recruiters read the second document first when you give them a reason to.
> <cite>Pranjul Rathour</cite>

## What did the first year look like?

**Foundations, and a community that did not exist yet. In 2023 I started the BCA and started TechVerse Enclave, a developer community that began as a place for a few of us to learn web development together and became, over three years, a 500-plus member community where I have mentored more than 200 students. The first year was Python, JavaScript, Git, one deployed page, and the habit of teaching what I had learned the week before.**



That roadmap is the one I gave 100+ first-years at the VSICS induction in July 2025, because it is the one that worked, not the one that sounds impressive [8].

## How did the community change things?

**More than anything else. TechVerse Enclave started as a hackathon team and a group chat and became the place where I learned to teach, to organise, to run sessions and to be known for something. Mentoring 200 students meant answering the same questions until I understood them properly. The sessions I ran inside the community became the sessions colleges invited me to give. The people in it became teammates, clients and referrals. Every later opportunity traces back to it.**


The story of the first 500 members, with what worked and what did not, is written up separately [4]. The short version: the community did not grow because I promoted it; it grew because sessions happened every week whether five people or fifty showed up.

## What did hackathons teach that classes did not?

**Scope, demos and losing. Three first prizes: Changethon 2025 at the National Social Summit, IIT Roorkee, with KrishGyan, voice-first farming advice over WhatsApp; Product Genesis at Vividhotsava 2025, CSJMU, with BrandHive; and BYTEBATTLE by MeetKats, with Annapurna, surplus food coordination. A top-three at IIT Kanpur. And STROT, which we did not win, because we built more and explained less than the team that did. The loss is the one I quote most in talks.**



Everything I now teach about hackathon strategy comes from those four rooms [5].

## How did the first clients and SCULT INDIA happen?

**Through the community and through shipping small things well. SCULT INDIA is an AI-first software agency; from 2024 I led engineering for it, architecture, UI/UX, deployment and delivery for a 14-member cross-functional team, and designed SCULT Studio CRM, the internal platform that runs projects, clients and operations [9]. The client products came one at a time, a pest-control business site in Goa, a music label, a digital library, a media company, and each one taught delivery under a deadline, which no college project can.**


Leading fourteen people while still a student is its own story, mostly about saying no and writing things down [6].


## How did the GenAI role come, and what did it produce?

**From the portfolio. NextUpgrad Web Solutions hired me as a GenAI engineer for February to July 2026 on the strength of shipped systems, and in those six months I independently designed, built and shipped five production AI applications: RAG.NextUpgrad, a retrieval platform with hybrid search, reranking, streaming citations and a confidence gate; FineTune Studio, a QLoRA fine-tuning platform with live telemetry; DocuLens AI, schema-validated document extraction with deterministic compliance scoring; FaceVision, browser-only face recognition and liveness that stores embeddings, never images; and the OCR & Speech Workspace, page-batched OCR, live speech-to-text and document chat with page citations. All with Docker, CI/CD, structured logging and metrics [1][10].**


Six months, five systems, because the habits, shipping weekly, testing, writing READMEs, evaluating honestly, were already three years old. The role did not create the habits. The habits created the role.

## What actually mattered, in order?

**Shipping small things every week. A community to learn and teach inside. Hackathons for scope and demos. Real clients for delivery. Writing in public so people could find the work. Reading the papers that mattered with a notebook open. Saying yes to every session and judging invitation early. Applying before I felt ready. Not: the college's name, certificates, or waiting for a placement cell.**



## What would I tell my first-year self?

**Start the community in month one, not month six. Post the first project even though it is embarrassing; the embarrassment is the point. Go to the hackathon two hours away. Learn to write a README before learning a fourth framework. Talk to the strangers at events. Ask for the client work. Read the papers, they are shorter than the tutorials. And stop comparing your college to the ones with placement cells; compare your GitHub to theirs.**


The longer letter is on the portfolio [8]. Most of it is the list above, said more gently.

## Was it worth it, and what is next?

**Yes. The year of shipping, 2025 into 2026, produced the systems, the team and the sessions, and it produced this site: a hundred pages answering the questions students and engineers actually search, written from what I built [7]. Next is more of the same at a larger scale: GenAI roles and products, more campuses, more judging panels, and a community that outgrows me. If you are in a first-year seat in a college nobody has heard of, the path is open, and the first step is a project this week.**





## Talk to me

**If you are at a college like mine and want the path explained in person, that is one of the sessions I give, free for student communities.** Email pranjulrathour41@gmail.com or use pranjulrathour.scult.in/invite. The projects are all public at github.com/Pranjulrathour [10].

# Where is the Gemini AI app? How to get it, use it, and is it safe
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/gemini-ai-app-guide/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-23

The Gemini AI app is Google's assistant, available as an official app on Android from Google Play, on iPhone from the App Store, and in any browser at gemini.google.com. On many Android phones it has replaced Google Assistant as the default assistant. This page explains where to get it, whether there is a Windows app, how to use it, what it is good for, whether it is free, how the app differs from Gemini models, example prompts, and how to use it safely and spot fake versions. Where is the Gemini AI app? On Android, get Gemini from Google Play; on iPhone, from the App Store; on a computer, open gemini.google.com in a browser. Check that the publisher is Google LLC before installing. Also asked as: where is gemini ai app On many newer Android phones Gemini is already installed and opens when you hold the power button or say "Hey Google", depending on settings. On iPhone, the Gemini app is standalone, and you can also reach Gemini features through the Google app. On a laptop or desktop, the web version has the same core features as the mobile app, including file uploads and longer conversations, which makes it the best place for study and coding work. Does Gemini have an app? Yes. Google publishes official Gemini apps for Android and iOS, and the full experience is available on the web. Gemini also appears inside Google products such as Gmail, Docs, Chrome and Android. The apps let you chat by text or voice, use the camera to ask about what you see, upload photos and files, generate images and use Gemini Live for back-and-forth voice conversations. Your conversations sync across devices when you are signed in to the same Google account. If your college or employer uses Google Workspace, Gemini may also be available in your work account with different rules set by the administrator. Does Gemini have a Windows app? Use Gemini on Windows through the browser at gemini.google.com. Chrome and Edge let you install the site as an app with its own window and taskbar icon, which works like a desktop app. In Chrome, open Gemini, open the menu and choose the option to install the page as an app; in Edge, use the Apps menu to install the site. Google has experimented with desktop apps that bring Gemini and AI search to Windows, so check Google's official download pages for anything current. Avoid third-party "Gemini for Windows" downloads from unknown websites; they are a common way to spread malware or steal Google account sessions. How do I use the Gemini app? Open the app, sign in with your Google account, and type or speak a request. Attach photos, files or screenshots with the plus button, and use Gemini Live for a voice conversation. Also asked as: how to gemini app use Tips that improve results: Give context: who you are, what you need and the format you want. Attach the material, such as lecture slides, a PDF or a photo of your notes. Use follow-ups to refine instead of starting over. Create a Gem, a custom assistant with saved instructions, for tasks you repeat. Turn on extensions such as Google Maps or YouTube when the answer needs them. Try one real task a day for a week: a summary, a study plan, an explanation, a draft email and a coding question. What is the Gemini app used for? People use the Gemini app to ask questions, learn and revise, write and edit, plan, summarise documents and videos, generate images, get coding help, and get answers about what the camera sees. Also asked as: what is gemini app used for Useful examples for students and developers: Explaining a concept with examples and quizzing you on it. Summarising a long PDF or a YouTube lecture. Planning a study schedule or trip with Google Maps and Calendar context. Drafting emails and reports, then making them shorter or more formal. Debugging an error message and explaining code. Deep Research for a cited overview of a topic. Its strongest advantage is integration with Google services you already use, such as Gmail, Drive, Docs, Maps and YouTube. Is the Gemini AI tool free? Yes. The Gemini app is free to use with a Google account, with daily limits on the most capable model and some features. Paid Google AI plans raise the limits and add features such as more advanced models, Deep Research capacity and video generation. Also asked as: is gemini ai tool free The free tier is enough for most learning and everyday tasks. Google has also run student offers and telecom partnerships in India that include paid plans at no cost for a period; check Google's official pages for current eligibility. Developers can use Gemini models through Google AI Studio with free quotas for prototyping. Watch out for websites selling "Gemini Pro" access; buy only through Google or official partners. What is the difference between Gemini models and the Gemini app? Gemini models are Google's family of AI models, in tiers such as Flash and Pro. The Gemini app is the consumer product built on those models, adding a chat interface, history, extensions, file handling and safety features. Also asked as: gemini models vs gemini app Developers use the models directly through the Gemini API or Google AI Studio, choosing a model, writing a system instruction and building their own interface. App users get Google's choices of model, tools and settings. The same model may behave differently in each place because of different instructions, tools and limits. If you are building a project, prototype prompts in AI Studio, where you can see and control the settings, rather than in the app. What is a good example of a Gemini AI prompt? A good prompt says who you are, what you want, the context and the format. For example: "I am a second-year BCA student. Explain how a hash table works with a simple example in Python, then give me three practice questions without answers." Also asked as: example gemini ai prompt More examples: "Summarise this PDF in ten bullet points for revision, then list five likely exam questions." "Here is my resume and a job description. List the skills I am missing and suggest one project for each." "Plan a seven-day study schedule for these four subjects; I can study three hours a day." "Look at this photo of my circuit and tell me what might be wrong." If an answer is too general, add constraints such as word count, audience or examples. Is the Gemini AI app safe? The official Gemini app is safe to install and use with normal care. Google applies security protections, but your conversations may be stored and, as Google states, some may be reviewed by trained reviewers to improve the service, so do not share confidential information. Also asked as: is gemini ai app safe Practical steps: review your Gemini activity settings to control how long conversations are saved and whether they are used to improve Google's services; delete conversations you no longer need; never enter passwords, OTPs, bank details or identity numbers; and check important answers, especially health, legal and financial ones, with official sources. On work accounts, your organisation's settings apply. Gemini can make mistakes, which the app itself notes. Is the Gemini app legit? Yes, the Gemini app published by Google LLC on Google Play and the App Store is legitimate and official. Fake apps and websites using the Gemini name also exist, so check the publisher and the website address. Also asked as: is gemini app legit Signs of a fake: a developer name other than Google LLC, requests to pay for "Gemini Pro" outside Google's own billing, websites that are not on google.com domains asking you to sign in, and downloads for Windows from unknown sites. Fake AI apps are a common way to steal accounts or show aggressive ads. If you installed something suspicious, uninstall it, change your Google password, and review your account's security and connected apps in your Google Account settings.

# Which Gemini API is free? Models, limits, billing and how to call it
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/gemini-api-free-tier/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-23

The free Gemini API is the Gemini Developer API used with a key from Google AI Studio: several Gemini models are available on a free tier with rate limits, and you pay only if you enable billing for higher limits or certain models. This page explains what is free and what is paid, the model tiers, why developers choose the Gemini API, how to call it, the API URL, when limits reset, how to give it internet access, and why responses can be slow. Which Google Gemini API is free? The Gemini Developer API, accessed with an API key from Google AI Studio, has a free tier. It covers several current models, typically the Flash and Flash-Lite tiers and sometimes Pro, within per-minute and per-day request limits. To start, sign in to Google AI Studio with a Google account, create an API key, and call the API from your code or test prompts in the Studio interface. The free tier is generous enough for learning, college projects and prototypes. Two conditions matter: limits are low for production traffic, and Google's terms say free-tier prompts and responses may be used to improve its products, so avoid sending sensitive data on the free tier. Vertex AI on Google Cloud is the enterprise route and is billed from the start, often with new-account credits. Is the Gemini API paid? It has both. The free tier costs nothing within its limits; the paid tier, enabled by linking a billing account, charges per token for input and output, with much higher rate limits and data that is not used to improve Google's products. Also asked as: is gemini api paid Paid usage is billed by tokens processed, with different rates for each model, for long prompts, and for extras such as grounding with search, context caching and media generation. You can set budgets and alerts in Google Cloud billing to avoid surprises. A practical path for students: build and test on the free tier, then enable billing only when you have real users or need higher limits. Check the pricing page for current rates, which change as models are released. Which Gemini API model is free? Most current Flash and Flash-Lite models are available on the free tier, and some Pro models have been offered with tight free limits. Image, video and audio generation models and the newest previews may be paid only. The rate-limits page in the documentation lists, for each model, the free-tier requests per minute, tokens per minute and requests per day, and AI Studio shows your project's current limits. Because Google rotates models, a model that is free today may be replaced or deprecated later, so avoid hard-coding assumptions; read the model name from configuration so you can switch quickly. For most projects, a Flash model is the best free choice: fast, capable and with the most room in its limits. What are the Gemini API models? The Gemini API offers model tiers: Flash-Lite for the cheapest, fastest high-volume tasks, Flash for most applications, and Pro for complex reasoning and coding. Specialised models cover embeddings, image generation, speech generation and live audio conversations. Each generation brings new versions of these tiers, with stable versions for production and preview versions for early access. Many models support thinking, where the model reasons before answering, with settings to control how much. Most accept text, images, audio, video and PDFs as input and support long context windows. The models page lists current names, context limits and capabilities; for embeddings, use the dedicated Gemini embedding model rather than a chat model. Why use the Gemini API? Developers choose the Gemini API for a generous free tier, strong multimodal input including video and long audio, very long context windows, built-in grounding with Google Search, and competitive pricing on Flash models. Also asked as: why use gemini api Good fits: Apps that analyse PDFs, images, audio or video in one call. High-volume tasks where Flash or Flash-Lite keeps costs low. Answers that need current web information through search grounding. Prototypes, since AI Studio lets you design and export prompts quickly. Weigh it like any provider: test quality on your own task, check latency from your users' region, and design for switching. In RAG.NextUpgrad I used multi-provider fallback, so one provider's outage or slowdown does not take the product down. How do I call the Gemini API? Install Google's official SDK, set your API key as an environment variable, and call generate_content with a model name and your prompt. Also asked as: how to call gemini api pip install google-genai export GEMINI_API_KEY=&quot;your-key&quot; from google import genai client = genai.Client() # reads GEMINI_API_KEY resp = client.models.generate_content( model=&quot;gemini-2.5-flash&quot;, contents=&quot;Explain retrieval-augmented generation in three sentences.&quot;, ) print(resp.text) The SDK also supports streaming, chat sessions, file uploads, structured JSON output with a schema, function calling and system instructions. SDKs exist for JavaScript, Go and Java too. Check the models page for the newest model names before you start a project. What is the Gemini API URL? The Gemini Developer API base URL is https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com. A typical request goes to /v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent, with your API key in the x-goog-api-key header. Also asked as: what is gemini api url A raw HTTP call looks like this: curl &quot;https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/gemini-2.5-flash:generateContent&quot; \ -H &quot;x-goog-api-key: $GEMINI_API_KEY&quot; -H &quot;Content-Type: application/json&quot; \ -d '{&quot;contents&quot;:[{&quot;parts&quot;:[{&quot;text&quot;:&quot;Hello&quot;}]}]}' Use streamGenerateContent for streaming responses, and the v1 path instead of v1beta when you only need stable features. Vertex AI uses a different, region-based endpoint on Google Cloud with service-account authentication instead of an API key. Never put your API key in front-end code or a mobile app, where anyone can extract it; call the API from your own backend and keep the key in an environment variable. When does the Gemini API limit reset? Daily request quotas reset at midnight Pacific time. Per-minute limits on requests and tokens work as rolling windows, so they recover within a minute of easing off. Also asked as: when does gemini api limit reset When you exceed a limit, the API returns a 429 error with a resource-exhausted status. Handle it with retries using exponential backoff and jitter, and queue work instead of sending bursts. To avoid hitting limits: cache repeated results, batch work where possible, use smaller models for simple tasks, and enable billing for higher tiers when you have real traffic. AI Studio shows your project's limits and usage, so check there before assuming you are blocked for other reasons. Can the Gemini API access the internet? Not by default, but you can enable grounding with Google Search as a tool. The model then searches when needed, answers with current information, and returns citations and search suggestions in the response metadata. Also asked as: can gemini api access internet Add the Google Search tool in your request configuration, and the model decides when to search. There is also a URL context tool that lets the model read specific web pages you provide. Grounding adds latency and may have separate pricing and limits, so enable it only for questions that need current information. Display the returned sources to users, both for trust and because Google's terms set requirements for showing search suggestions. Why is the Gemini API slow? Responses slow down because of thinking time on reasoning-capable models, long prompts or files, large outputs, search grounding, peak load, or network distance. Each has a fix. Also asked as: why gemini api is slow Ways to speed it up: Lower or disable the thinking budget for simple tasks, or use Flash-Lite. Stream responses so users see text immediately. Shorten prompts and send only relevant context; cache repeated long context. Limit the maximum output tokens to what you need. Use grounding only when current information is required. Measure latency per step to find the actual bottleneck. If slowness is sudden and widespread, check Google's status pages and retry with backoff.

# What does Gemini Canvas do? Notebooks, models and how Gemini helps users
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/gemini-canvas-notebooks-models/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-23

Gemini Canvas is a workspace inside the Gemini app where you write and edit documents or code alongside Gemini, with the draft in its own panel and live previews for web code. Notebooks, in Google's ecosystem, usually means NotebookLM, which answers questions only from the sources you upload. This page explains how both work, which Gemini model to pick for general work and for coding, when Gemini launched worldwide and in India, and how Gemini helps draft emails in Gmail and slides in Google Slides. What does Gemini Canvas do? Canvas gives you a dedicated editing space next to the chat. Gemini writes a document or code there, and you refine it together: highlight a section to change, adjust tone or length, or run and preview code such as a web page. It is useful for longer pieces you will iterate on: an essay outline, a project report, a cover letter, a Python script or a small HTML app. For code, Canvas can show a live preview of web projects, so you can see a landing page or a simple game working and ask for changes. Canvas can also turn content into other formats, such as a web page or quiz, and export documents to Google Docs. It replaces the clumsy pattern of copying code from the chat into a file and back. How does Gemini Canvas work? Select Canvas in the Gemini prompt bar, describe what you want, and Gemini opens the draft in a side panel. You then chat to revise it, or edit the draft directly, and Gemini updates the canvas rather than writing a new answer each time. Useful moves inside Canvas: Highlight a paragraph and ask for it to be simpler, shorter or more formal. Ask for a specific change: "add error handling to the fetch call". Preview web code and describe what looks wrong. Export a document to Google Docs to keep editing there. Keep the scope small, one document or one small app per canvas, and save versions you like before asking for big changes. What are Gemini notebooks? In Google's AI tools, notebooks usually refer to NotebookLM: a research assistant where you create a notebook, add sources such as PDFs, Google Docs, websites or YouTube videos, and ask questions that are answered only from those sources, with citations. Google has been connecting NotebookLM with the Gemini app, so you can work with notebook material inside Gemini as well. For students, NotebookLM is one of the best free study tools: add your lecture notes, textbook chapters and past papers, then ask for summaries, explanations, study guides or quizzes. Because answers come from your sources and link to the exact passages, they are easier to trust and check than general chatbot answers. It also creates audio overviews, a podcast-style discussion of your material. How do Gemini notebooks work? You create a notebook in NotebookLM, upload or link sources, and ask questions. NotebookLM retrieves the relevant passages from your sources and has Gemini answer from them, citing each claim back to the source text. This is retrieval-augmented generation scoped to your own material, the same principle behind the document chat I built in the OCR &amp; Speech Workspace, where answers cite page numbers. Tips: keep one notebook per subject or project, add only sources you trust, and ask specific questions such as "compare the two definitions of normalisation in these notes". Click the citations to verify. Generated study guides and quizzes are good for revision, but check them against the sources before an exam. Which Gemini model is best? For everyday tasks, Flash is best: fast and capable. For hard problems such as complex coding, maths and analysis, the Pro tier or a thinking mode is best. The newest generation of each tier is usually better than the previous one. The Gemini app chooses a model automatically unless you pick one, and the options shown depend on your plan. Developers choose explicitly in the Gemini API: Flash-Lite for the cheapest high-volume tasks, Flash as the default for most products, and Pro for the hardest requests. A good production pattern is to start with Flash, measure where it fails, and route only those cases to Pro. Google's models page lists the current versions, which change several times a year. Which Gemini model is best for coding? Use the most capable Pro model available to you, ideally with thinking enabled, for debugging, architecture and multi-file changes. Flash is fine for quick snippets, explanations and simple scripts. For real projects, the model matters less than the tool. Google's coding tools, such as Gemini CLI, Gemini Code Assist in your editor and Antigravity, can read your whole project, run commands and tests, and propose edits, which makes their output far more reliable than code from a chat window. Whatever you use, give precise tasks, include error messages, keep a project context file with build and test commands, and review every change. Compare against other coding tools on one real task before settling. When was Gemini AI launched? Google announced the Gemini model family in December 2023. Its chatbot Bard, launched in early 2023, was renamed Gemini in February 2024, when the Gemini app also arrived on Android and iPhone. Also asked as: when gemini ai was launched · when gemini launched in india Since then Google has released several model generations with improvements in reasoning, coding, long context and multimodal understanding, added Gemini to Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Android and Chrome, and launched developer tools including AI Studio, the Gemini API, Gemini CLI and Antigravity. The technical report on the first generation describes models trained to handle text, images, audio and video together, a design choice that shapes how Gemini works with media today. When did Gemini launch in India? Google's AI chatbot was available in India from 2023, under the Bard name, and the Gemini app launched in India in 2024 with support for English and several Indian languages. Language support has expanded since, and Gemini works in Hindi, Bengali, Tamil, Telugu, Marathi, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam and Urdu, among others, which makes it useful for students and users more comfortable in their own language. Google has also run offers in India, including free plans for eligible students and a partnership with Jio. On Android phones in India, Gemini increasingly replaces Google Assistant as the default assistant. Check Google's Gemini help pages for the current list of languages and features. How does Gemini help users draft an email? In Gmail, Gemini drafts an email from a short prompt with "Help me write", suggests replies in context, and can refine a draft to be more formal, shorter or more detailed. It can also summarise a long thread before you reply. Also asked as: how does gemini assist users in drafting an email Write prompts that include the recipient, purpose and tone, for example "email my professor asking for a two-day extension for the project, polite and brief, mention I was unwell". Review the draft for facts: Gemini may add details or commitments you did not intend. For important emails, read it aloud once; if it does not sound like you, edit it. In Google Workspace accounts, administrators control which Gemini features are available. How does Gemini AI help users in slide creation? In Google Slides, Gemini can generate slide content and layouts from a prompt, create images for slides, and help rewrite text. It speeds up the first draft, while you still shape the story and check every fact. A good workflow: write a one-paragraph brief for the deck, its audience and key message; ask Gemini for an outline of eight to ten slides; generate slides one at a time and edit them; add your own data, screenshots and examples; and cut words, since slides work best with very little text. For college presentations, prepare speaker notes in your own words, because evaluators ask questions about what you present. Gemini-generated images should be labelled when they could be mistaken for real photos.

# What is Gemini CLI, and why do Gemini, ChatGPT, Claude and Cursor have limits?
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/gemini-cli-and-ai-limits/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-23

Gemini CLI is Google's open-source AI agent for the command line. You run it in a project folder, describe a task, and it uses Gemini models to read files, run commands and make edits, asking for approval as it goes. It competes with Claude Code, OpenAI's Codex CLI and GitHub Copilot CLI. The second half of this page explains why Gemini, ChatGPT, Claude and Cursor all limit how much you can use them, including file and image uploads, and how to work within those limits. Gemini CLI vs other coding CLIs: how do they compare? Gemini CLI, Claude Code, OpenAI's Codex CLI and GitHub Copilot CLI are all terminal agents that read your codebase, edit files and run commands. They differ mainly in the models behind them, pricing and free tiers, and extras such as integrations. Gemini CLI is open source and offers a free tier with a personal Google account, which makes it popular with students. Claude Code is widely used for complex multi-file work and has a large ecosystem of extensions. Codex CLI is open source and works with a ChatGPT plan or API key. Copilot CLI fits teams already on GitHub Copilot. All support the Model Context Protocol for extra tools. The honest way to choose is one real task in your own repository with each, judged on correctness and how much fixing the result needs. How does Gemini CLI work? Gemini CLI runs a reason-and-act loop: it reads your request, decides which tool to use, such as reading a file, searching code, running a shell command or fetching a web page, observes the result, and repeats until the task is done. Also asked as: vs gemini cli Built-in tools cover the file system, shell commands, web fetch and Google Search grounding, and you can add more through MCP servers. A GEMINI.md file in your project gives it persistent context: build commands, conventions and rules. Before risky actions such as editing files or running commands, it asks for confirmation unless you change that setting. Because it sees your whole project and can run tests, its changes are more likely to work than code pasted from a chat window, but every diff still needs review. Is there a Gemini CLI tutorial? Yes. The official repository's documentation covers installation and features, and a first session takes about ten minutes. Also asked as: tutorial gemini cli npm install -g @google/gemini-cli cd my-project gemini Sign in with your Google account when prompted, then try: "Explain this project's structure and how to run the tests." Create a GEMINI.md with the test command and coding rules. "Add input validation to the signup route and write a test for it." Review each proposed edit and command before approving. Run the tests yourself and commit. Work in a Git repository so you can roll back anything you do not like. Is there a course for Gemini CLI? Google's official documentation and codelabs are the best free starting points, and some online learning platforms offer short courses on Gemini CLI and AI coding agents. A course matters less than using the tool on a real project. Also asked as: course gemini cli Look for courses that teach transferable skills: writing a good context file, breaking work into small tasks, connecting MCP servers, reviewing diffs and testing agent output. Those apply equally to Claude Code, Codex and Copilot. A practical self-made course: spend a week building a small FastAPI or Next.js app entirely through an agent, keeping notes on which prompts worked, where it went wrong and how you fixed it. That record is also good material for interviews and a blog post. Can Gemini CLI handle a complex RAG migration? It can help a lot with a complex migration, such as moving a RAG system to a new vector store, embedding model or framework, if you break the work into stages, keep tests at every step and review each change. Also asked as: how i used gemini cli to orchestrate a complex rag migration A workable plan for any coding agent: Write the migration plan first and save it in the repository. Build an evaluation set of questions with known good answers before changing anything. Migrate one component at a time: ingestion, embeddings, index, retrieval, generation. After each stage, re-run the evaluation and compare retrieval recall and answer quality. Keep the old path working behind a flag until the new one matches it. When I built RAG.NextUpgrad, the evaluation set was what made changes safe; without one, an agent can produce a migration that looks clean but quietly retrieves worse passages. Does Gemini have a limit? Yes. The Gemini app has daily limits on prompts with the most capable models and on features such as Deep Research, image and video generation. Free accounts have lower limits than paid Google AI plans, and the API has separate rate limits. When you reach a limit, Gemini usually switches to a faster model or tells you when the limit resets. Limits are counted per feature, so you might still use the fast model after exhausting the Pro allowance. Google lists the current limits in the Gemini Apps help centre, and they change as plans are updated. Developers using AI Studio or the Gemini API see rate limits per minute and per day for their project, which rise with paid usage tiers. Does Gemini have a limit for uploading images? Yes. Gemini limits how many files and images you can upload per prompt and the maximum file size, and some limits differ between free and paid plans. The Gemini Apps help centre lists the current numbers. If an upload fails, reduce the number of images per message, compress large photos, or combine screenshots into one image or PDF. For many pages of notes, a single PDF often works better than many photos. Image generation also has its own daily limit, separate from uploads. Developers using the Gemini API have different limits for inline images versus files uploaded through the Files API, which suits larger media. Check the documentation for the version you are using. Why does ChatGPT have a limit? ChatGPT has limits because every reply uses expensive computing power, especially with the most capable and reasoning models. Limits share capacity fairly among users, keep the service responsive at busy times, and separate free and paid tiers. Different features have separate limits: messages with advanced models, image generation, deep research, file uploads and agent tasks. When you hit one, ChatGPT may switch you to a lighter model until the limit resets. To get more from your allowance, write one clear, complete prompt instead of many small follow-ups, use the faster model for simple tasks, and start new chats instead of extending very long ones, which cost more to process. OpenAI's help centre lists the current limits per plan. Why does Claude AI have a limit? Claude has usage limits because running large models costs significant computing resources, and longer conversations cost more, since Claude rereads the whole conversation with each reply. Limits keep the service available for everyone. Claude's limits are measured over rolling time windows, and long chats with large attachments use your allowance faster than short ones. To stretch it: start a new chat for each task, use Projects to hold reference files instead of re-uploading them, keep prompts focused, and choose a lighter model for simple work. Paid plans raise limits substantially, and Claude Code usage counts against the same plan. Developers using the API pay per token and have rate limits that rise with usage tiers. Does Cursor AI have a limit? Yes. Cursor's plans include a usage allowance for AI requests, with the most capable models costing more of it per request. Free plans have tighter limits, and paid plans include more, with options to pay for extra usage. Also asked as: does cursor ai have limit Cursor has changed how it meters usage more than once, so check its pricing page and the usage dashboard in your account for the current rules. Agent sessions with large context and premium models use the allowance fastest. To make it last, select a cheaper model for routine edits, point the agent at the right files rather than the whole repository, use a .cursorignore file to keep build outputs and data out of context, and keep sessions focused on one task.

# What is Gemini Live? Using Gemini on your phone, and Gemini tutorials
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/gemini-live-and-phone-guide/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-23

Gemini Live is the real-time voice mode of Google's Gemini assistant: you talk naturally, interrupt whenever you like, and Gemini answers out loud; you can also share your camera or screen so it can see what you are looking at. On Android it is built into the phone's assistant; on iPhone it is in the Gemini app. This page explains how Live works, how to find and use Gemini on your phone, whether you can remove it, and short tutorials for Gemini in general, PDFs, Veo video generation and notebooks. What is Gemini Live? Gemini Live is a conversational voice mode where you speak with Gemini in real time, as in a phone call. You can interrupt it, change topic, and ask follow-ups, and it keeps the conversation's context. Live also lets you share your camera, so Gemini can talk about what it sees, such as a plant, a circuit board or a menu in another language, and your screen, so it can help with what you are looking at. It is useful for practising interviews or spoken English, brainstorming while walking, learning a topic by asking questions aloud, or getting help with something physical in front of you. Transcripts of Live conversations appear in your Gemini history. How does Gemini Live work? Gemini Live streams your voice to Google's servers, where a Gemini model built for low-latency audio understands speech and generates a spoken reply, while listening for interruptions. Camera and screen sharing add a live video feed to the conversation. Because it is designed for conversation, it uses natural turn-taking: it stops when you start speaking and picks up from where you interrupted. It needs an internet connection and uses mobile data, so expect higher data use on video. Voice options are in settings. Developers can build similar real-time voice and video experiences with the Gemini Live API. As with any assistant, check important facts it states aloud, since spoken answers are harder to verify at a glance. Where is Gemini on my phone? On most recent Android phones, Gemini is the default assistant: hold the power button, swipe up from a bottom corner, or say "Hey Google". It is also an app called Gemini in your app drawer. On iPhone, open the Gemini app from the App Store. Also asked as: where&#x27;s gemini on my phone If you do not see it on Android, update the Google app and Play Store apps, or install Gemini from Google Play. Some phones, such as certain Samsung models, also add a Gemini shortcut to the side button. On iPhone you can add Gemini to the Lock Screen or use a Shortcut to open it quickly. Make sure you install the official app published by Google LLC; fake "Gemini" apps exist. How do I use Gemini on an Android phone? Open Gemini from the power button, a corner swipe or the app, then type, speak or tap the Live button for a voice conversation. Use the camera and screen options to ask about what you see. Also asked as: how to gemini on an android phone Things worth trying: "Summarise this page" while a long article is on screen. Circle to Search on supported phones to ask about anything on screen. "Set a reminder to submit the assignment at 6 pm tomorrow." Photograph your notes and ask for a summary or quiz. Ask about a YouTube video while it plays, where supported. Connected apps, such as Google Maps, Calendar, Keep and YouTube, let Gemini act on your behalf. Review which apps it can access in Gemini's settings. How does Gemini work on my phone? Gemini on your phone sends your requests to Google's Gemini models in the cloud, uses on-device models for some quick features, and connects to apps such as Calendar, Messages, Maps and YouTube when you allow it. Most answers come from cloud models, so an internet connection is needed. Some phones also run Gemini Nano, a small on-device model, for features such as summarising recordings or smart replies, which work faster and keep data on the device. When you ask Gemini to do something in another app, it uses that app's permissions. Your conversations are saved to your Google account according to your activity settings, which you can change or turn off in Gemini's privacy settings. Can I remove Gemini from my phone? On most Android phones you can switch the default digital assistant away from Gemini in settings, and disable or uninstall the Gemini app. Whether you can fully remove it depends on your phone and Android version. Look in Settings, then Apps, then Default apps, then Digital assistant app, to change the assistant. To stop Gemini opening from the power button, change the power button setting. If the Gemini app came preinstalled as a system app, you may only be able to disable it or uninstall its updates. Google has been replacing Google Assistant with Gemini on Android, so switching back may not be available on every device. On iPhone, simply delete the app. Is there a Gemini tutorial for beginners? Yes. Google's Gemini help centre has guides for each feature, and the fastest way to learn is to try five everyday tasks in your first week. Also asked as: tutorial gemini · tutorial gemini notebook A beginner's week: Day 1: ask Gemini to explain a topic you are studying and quiz you. Day 2: upload a PDF and ask for a one-page summary. Day 3: use Gemini Live to practise answering interview questions aloud. Day 4: create a Gem, a custom assistant with saved instructions, for a task you repeat. Day 5: connect Google Calendar and plan your week. Write prompts with context: who you are, what you need and the format you want. Check facts in every answer. How do I use Gemini with a PDF? Upload the PDF in the Gemini app with the plus button, then ask questions: a summary, explanations of difficult sections, key terms, or practice questions. Gemini can read long documents and point you to relevant parts. Also asked as: tutorial gemini pdf Good prompts for study: "Summarise this chapter in ten bullet points for revision." "Explain section 3.2 as if I am new to the topic, with an example." "List all definitions in this PDF as a glossary." "Write five exam-style questions from this document, then check my answers." For scanned PDFs, Gemini can read the images, but accuracy drops with poor scans. For courses with many documents, NotebookLM is often better, because it keeps sources together and cites the exact passages. How do I use Veo 3 in Gemini? In the Gemini app, choose the video option, describe the scene you want, and Gemini generates a short clip with Google's Veo model, including sound. Access depends on your plan and country, and there are daily limits. Also asked as: tutorial gemini veo 3 Write prompts like a director: subject, action, setting, camera movement, lighting, style and sound, for example "a slow dolly shot of a student coding at night in a small hostel room, warm desk lamp, rain on the window, soft keyboard sounds". Generate several versions and keep the best. Clips are short, so plan longer videos as several shots edited together. Generated videos carry a visible or invisible watermark; label them as AI-generated when you share them, and never create videos of real people without consent. How do I use Gemini notebooks? Notebooks in Google's AI tools usually means NotebookLM: create a notebook, add sources such as PDFs, Docs, websites or YouTube videos, then ask questions answered only from those sources, with citations. Google has also been connecting notebooks to the Gemini app. A study workflow: create one notebook per subject, add your syllabus, lecture notes and textbook chapters, and ask for a study guide, a list of likely exam questions, and explanations of the hardest topics. Click citations to check each answer against your material. Audio overviews turn your sources into a podcast-style discussion you can listen to while travelling. Keep sources accurate and current, because answers are only as good as what you upload.

# How to get Gemini Pro for free, and what Gemini Pro offers
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/gemini-pro-free-guide/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-23

You can use Gemini Pro for free in three ways: the free Gemini app gives limited access to Google's Pro model, Google AI Studio lets developers try Pro models with free quotas, and Google has run time-limited offers that include the paid Google AI Pro plan at no cost for eligible students and for some telecom customers in India, such as Jio users. This page explains those routes, what the Pro plan adds, how Gemini, Flash, Pro and thinking modes differ, daily limits, family sharing, and how Gemini relates to Antigravity. How can I get Gemini Pro for free? Use the free Gemini app, which includes limited access to the Pro model, use Google AI Studio for free developer access, or claim an official offer that includes Google AI Pro at no cost if you are eligible. Also asked as: how to gemini pro for free The options in order of effort: Free Gemini app: sign in at gemini.google.com or the mobile app; free accounts get some Pro model use with lower limits. Google AI Studio: a developer playground where you can try current models, including Pro, with free usage quotas. Official offers: Google has run student offers and telecom partnerships that include the paid plan for a limited period. Offers change often, so confirm eligibility on Google's own pages. Avoid "free Gemini Pro" links shared in groups; they are a common route for phishing and account theft. Is Gemini Pro free for students? Google has offered its paid AI plan free for a limited period to students in several countries, including India, through verification with a college email or student ID. Whether an offer is open today depends on the country and date. When an offer is live, you sign in with a personal Google account, verify student status through Google's verification partner, and the plan is applied for the stated period. It usually renews at the normal rate afterwards unless you cancel, so note the end date. Even without an offer, students can do a lot on the free tier: explaining concepts, debugging code, summarising lecture notes and planning projects. NotebookLM, also from Google, is free and very good for studying from your own notes and papers. How do I get Gemini Pro with Jio? Reliance Jio and Google announced a partnership in 2025 that gives eligible Jio users access to Google AI Pro at no cost for a limited period. Eligible users claim it from the MyJio app with the Google account they want to use. Also asked as: how to gemini pro with jio Open the MyJio app, look for the Google Gemini or Google AI Pro offer banner, check the eligibility conditions, which have depended on age group and plan, and follow the steps to link your Google account. The benefit then appears in the Gemini app and Google One. Rules, eligible plans and duration are set by Jio and Google and have changed since launch, so rely on the MyJio app and Google's announcement, not on screenshots shared online. Never enter OTPs or passwords on links that claim to unlock the offer. What does Gemini Pro offer? The Google AI Pro plan gives higher access to Google's most capable Gemini models, longer context for big files, Deep Research, video and image generation with higher limits, Gemini inside Gmail and Docs, NotebookLM with higher limits, and extra cloud storage. For students and developers the useful parts are: More use of the Pro model and thinking modes for hard maths and code. Deep Research, which browses many sources and writes a cited report. Uploading long PDFs and codebases thanks to a large context window. Gemini in Gmail, Docs and Sheets for drafting and analysis. Higher limits in Google's coding tools. The exact feature list and limits change as Google updates the plan, so check the plan page on Google One. If you mostly ask quick questions, the free tier is enough. What is the difference between Gemini and Gemini Pro? Gemini is Google's family of AI models and the name of its assistant app. Gemini Pro refers either to the Pro model, the most capable tier in a Gemini generation, or to the Google AI Pro subscription that gives more access to it. The model family has tiers: Flash-Lite for the cheapest, fastest tasks, Flash for most everyday work, and Pro for complex reasoning and coding. Some generations also add a deeper thinking mode on top. The Gemini app picks a model for you unless you choose one. The subscription changes your limits and features, not the model itself: a free user and a paid user asking the Pro model the same question get the same quality of answer, but the free user runs out sooner. What is the difference between Gemini Flash and Pro? Flash is the faster, cheaper model tuned for everyday tasks and high volume. Pro is the more capable model for complex reasoning, difficult code and long multi-step work, and it is slower and more expensive per request. In practice: Use Flash for summaries, emails, quick explanations, extraction from documents and chat features in your app. Use Pro for debugging a tricky bug, designing a system, solving hard maths, or long analysis where a wrong step costs more than waiting. For developers building with the Gemini API, Flash is usually the right default because latency and cost matter at scale. Start with Flash, measure where it fails, and route only those cases to Pro. That routing pattern is how most production AI apps keep costs under control. When should I use Gemini Pro vs thinking mode? Pro is a model tier; thinking is a way of running a model, where it reasons step by step before answering. Use a thinking mode when the task needs several steps of logic, and a standard fast mode when it does not. Also asked as: when to use gemini pro vs thinking Thinking helps with maths and physics problems, competitive programming, debugging, planning a project and comparing options with many constraints. It adds waiting time and uses more of your limits, so it is wasted on simple questions, rewriting text or quick facts. If an answer from the fast mode seems shallow or contradicts itself, rerun the same prompt with thinking on. For developers, the Gemini API exposes thinking controls on models that support it, so you can set how much reasoning to spend per request. How many Gemini Pro queries do I get per day? It depends on your plan: free accounts get a small daily allowance of Pro model prompts, and paid plans get much more. Google lists the current limits in the Gemini Apps help centre, and they change from time to time. Also asked as: how many gemini pro queries per day Limits are also counted per feature: Pro model prompts, Deep Research reports, image generation and video generation each have their own allowance. When you reach a limit, the app usually falls back to a faster model or asks you to wait. To stretch a free allowance, use Flash for routine tasks, write one clear, complete prompt instead of many short follow-ups, and save Pro and thinking for the problems that need them. Developers using the API have separate rate limits shown in Google AI Studio. Can I share Gemini Pro with family? Partly. Google AI Pro is a Google One plan, and its cloud storage can be shared with up to five family members in a Google One family group. Whether the Gemini features are shared too depends on the plan and country. Set up a family group from your Google account, invite members, then enable sharing in Google One settings. Each member keeps their own private files and chats; sharing never exposes your Gemini conversations or Drive files to others. Google has been extending AI benefits to family members in some regions, so check the Google One help pages for your country before assuming everyone in the group gets Pro features. Offer-based plans, such as student or telecom offers, may have their own sharing rules. Does Gemini Pro include Antigravity? Antigravity is Google's agent-first coding environment and is offered separately from the Gemini app. Individuals have been able to use it without a paid plan within rate limits, and Google AI subscriptions have come with higher limits. Antigravity runs coding agents that plan and carry out tasks across an editor, a terminal and a browser, using Gemini models and some models from other providers. Because it is new, its pricing, limits and the benefits attached to Google AI plans have changed several times, so check Google's Antigravity site and the plan page before deciding. For learning to code with AI, the free options, such as Antigravity's free limits, Gemini in the browser, or Gemini Code Assist's free tier for individuals, are usually enough.

# Why does Gemini add a watermark? SynthID, images, text, and who owns Gemini
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/gemini-watermark-synthid/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-23

Gemini adds watermarks so that images, video and audio it generates can be recognised as AI-made. Many images carry a small visible Gemini mark, and Google embeds an invisible digital watermark called SynthID in generated media, designed to survive cropping, compression and filters. This page explains why, how it applies to edited photos and to text, how to check for watermarks, why removing them is a bad idea, who made and owns Gemini, and the real risks of using it. Why does Gemini add a watermark? To make AI-generated content identifiable. As generated images and videos become realistic, watermarks help people, platforms and fact-checkers tell synthetic media from real photos and footage, reducing misinformation and misuse. Also asked as: why does gemini leave a watermark Google uses two layers. A visible mark tells viewers at a glance that an image came from Gemini. SynthID, developed by Google DeepMind, embeds an imperceptible signal in the content that detection tools can read even after common edits. Google has also joined industry efforts on content provenance, such as the C2PA standard, which attaches information about how content was made. Watermarking is part of responsible deployment and increasingly expected by platforms and regulators. Why does Gemini add a watermark to images? Generated and AI-edited images can be mistaken for real photos, so Gemini marks them. A visible watermark appears on many images created in the Gemini app, and SynthID is embedded invisibly in the pixels. The invisible watermark matters more than the visible one: a logo can be cropped out, but SynthID is designed to remain detectable after resizing, compression, colour changes and screenshots, though no watermark is impossible to defeat. Whether a visible mark appears can depend on the product, plan and feature, and Google has changed this over time. For professional use, check the current terms for your plan, and in any case disclose that an image is AI-generated when it could mislead. Does Gemini put a watermark on photos you edit? Yes. When Gemini edits a photo with AI, the result is treated as AI-generated or AI-modified media and receives SynthID, and often a visible mark, even though it started as your own photo. That is intentional: an edited photo with a changed background, added objects or altered faces is exactly the kind of image that could mislead if presented as unedited. For harmless uses, such as a cleaner background for a project poster, the watermark simply records the edit. For official documents, such as ID or passport photos, do not use AI edits at all; use a real photo and approved tools. Never edit images of other people in ways they have not agreed to. Does Gemini add a watermark to text? Google has developed SynthID for text, which subtly adjusts how the model chooses words to embed a statistical signal, and it has applied this in its Gemini products. Unlike images, text watermarks are fragile and do not prove authorship. Also asked as: does gemini add watermark to text · does gemini put a watermark on text Text watermarking works by nudging token choices in a way that is invisible to readers but detectable statistically over enough text. Heavy editing, paraphrasing, translation or very short passages weaken the signal. Google published the method and open-sourced a version for developers. For students, the key point is that neither watermarks nor "AI detectors" are reliable judges of whether an essay was AI-written; follow your college's rules on AI use and be transparent about how you used it. Can you tell if text was written by Gemini? Not reliably by reading it, and not reliably with public AI detectors, which produce many false positives, including on genuine human writing. SynthID text detection exists, but it needs access to the watermark scheme and enough unedited text. Signs often cited, such as generic phrasing, certain words or very even structure, appear in human writing too, so they are weak evidence. If you are a teacher or reviewer, ask the writer to explain their work, show drafts or discuss the topic; understanding is the real test. If you are a student using AI, keep your notes and drafts, write in your own voice, and declare AI assistance where required. Accusations based only on detector scores are unfair and often wrong. How do I check for a Gemini watermark? Look for the visible Gemini mark on the image, and use Google's SynthID verification tools, which Google has made available for checking whether content contains its watermark, including through the Gemini app for images. Upload or share the image to the verification feature and it reports whether SynthID was detected. A negative result does not prove an image is real: it may come from another AI tool that uses no watermark, or the watermark may have been damaged. Provenance metadata under the C2PA standard can also show an image's history where supported. For news and claims that matter, combine tools with traditional checks: reverse image search, the original source and context. What is the best Gemini watermark remover? Removing watermarks to hide that an image is AI-generated is deceptive, can break Google's terms of use, and may break platform rules or laws in some places, so this page does not recommend tools for it. The invisible SynthID watermark is also designed to survive most edits. If the visible mark gets in the way of a legitimate use, better options are: check whether your plan or a different Google tool offers outputs suited to professional use; generate the image with enough margin and compose it in a design tool without hiding its origin; or use stock photos or your own photography where a real image is needed. Labelling content as AI-generated is increasingly expected and builds trust with your audience. Who made Gemini? Gemini was made by Google DeepMind, Google's AI research lab, formed in 2023 by merging Google Brain and DeepMind. Google announced the first Gemini models in December 2023. The models were developed by large teams across Google DeepMind and Google Research, building on Google's earlier work, including the Transformer architecture published by Google researchers in 2017. The Gemini app, previously called Bard, is built by Google's product teams on these models. Gemini models are also available to developers through Google AI Studio, the Gemini API and Vertex AI on Google Cloud. Who owns Gemini? Google owns Gemini. Google is a subsidiary of Alphabet Inc., so Alphabet is the ultimate parent company. Gemini products follow Google's terms of service and privacy policy. That ownership matters for data: conversations in the Gemini app are stored in your Google account according to your activity settings and may be reviewed to improve services, as Google discloses; work and school accounts follow their organisation's Google Workspace settings. Developers using the Gemini API agree to Google's API terms, which differ between free and paid tiers. Read those terms before sending sensitive information. Is Gemini dangerous? Gemini is not dangerous in itself, but like any powerful AI tool it has real risks: confident wrong answers, privacy exposure if you share sensitive data, realistic fake images in the wrong hands, and over-reliance that weakens your own skills. Also asked as: why gemini is dangerous Use it safely: Verify facts, especially health, legal and financial information, with official sources. Keep passwords, OTPs, identity numbers and other people's private information out of chats. Review activity settings and delete conversations you do not need kept. Label AI-generated images and never create misleading images of real people. Use it to learn faster, not to skip learning. Google applies safety filters and watermarking, but responsible use is still up to you.

# GenAI and LLM interview questions with answers: RAG, fine-tuning, prompting, agents, evaluation and system design, from both sides of the table
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/genai-interview-questions/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-09-24

## What do GenAI engineer interviews actually ask?

**Six things, in some order: LLM fundamentals, tokens, context, attention, hallucination; RAG, how you build and evaluate retrieval; fine-tuning, when and how with LoRA; prompting and agents, including safety; evaluation and cost, how you know it works and what it costs; and one system design where you assemble the pieces. Plus a walkthrough of a project you built, which is where most decisions get made. Definitions get you past the first minute. Trade-offs and stories get you the offer.**


I have sat on both sides: interviewing candidates for SCULT INDIA and being interviewed for GenAI roles. The pattern is consistent enough that this page is the preparation I now give mentees, with the answers I would want to hear. Longer notes are on the portfolio [11][12].

> The question is never really "what is RAG". The question is "have you built one, and do you know what broke". Answer the second question every time.
> <cite>Pranjul Rathour</cite>

## LLM fundamentals: what will they ask?

**Expect: what is a token and why does it matter for cost; what is the context window and one failure mode of long contexts; explain attention in one minute; what is hallucination and how do you manage it; open-weight versus API models for a given product; what is the difference between a base model and an instruct model. Answer each with the concept in one sentence, then a consequence for a product you built.**



## RAG interview questions

**Expect: explain RAG end to end; why is chunking important and how do you choose a size; why add keyword search to embeddings; what does a reranker do; how do you evaluate retrieval separately from generation; how do you stop the model answering when the documents do not contain the answer; how would you handle multi-tenant documents. Every question maps to a stage of the pipeline; know the pipeline and you know the questions.**



The paper to cite is Lewis et al. [1]; the metric framework most interviewers know is RAGAS [7]. The answer that separates candidates is to the evaluation question: "I measure retrieval recall on twenty labelled questions before I look at a single generated answer, because a system can be faithful to the wrong passage."

## Fine-tuning interview questions

**Expect: when would you fine-tune instead of using RAG; explain LoRA and QLoRA; how do you prepare a dataset; how do you read a loss curve; what is catastrophic forgetting; how do you evaluate a fine-tuned model honestly; can you fine-tune GPT. The trap question is "how would you teach the model our product facts", and the right answer is "I would not, I would retrieve them, and fine-tune only for the voice and format".**



## Prompt engineering and agent interview questions

**Expect: system prompt versus user prompt and why the split matters for security; what is prompt injection and how do you limit its damage; when does chain-of-thought help and when does it waste tokens; how do you test a prompt; what is an agent and where does the model's judgement actually belong; how would you stop an agent taking a harmful action; when is a workflow better than an agent. Safety questions are where candidates who have only prototyped get exposed.**


The references interviewers respect: chain-of-thought [5], ReAct for agents [6], OWASP for security [9], and Anthropic's guide for the workflow-versus-agent distinction [10]. The answer to "how do you stop a harmful action" is not a clever prompt; it is least-privilege tools and a human confirmation for anything irreversible.


## Evaluation and cost questions

**Expect: how do you know your system works; what metrics do you track; how do you test a prompt change before deploying; how much does this feature cost per month; how would you cut that cost in half; what do you log. The interviewer is testing whether you treat an LLM system like software. Answer with a fixed evaluation set, metrics per stage, a CI check, tokens logged per request, and a cost model: input plus output tokens times price times requests.**



## System design questions for GenAI roles

**Expect one design in 30 to 45 minutes: a support chatbot over company documents, a document extraction service, a coding assistant, a voice assistant for a regional language. Structure it: clarify users and constraints, draw the request path, name each component and its failure mode, say what you would measure, estimate cost, and state what you would cut for version one. Interviewers grade the trade-offs you name unprompted, not the boxes you draw.**



## Behavioural and project questions

**Expect: tell me about a project; what broke and what did you do; a time you disagreed with a technical decision; how you handle a requirement you think is wrong; why this role. For the project question, use one project and go deep: the problem, the decision you made, the failure you hit, the fix, the measured result. My RAG platform's confidence gate exists because of a failure; that story has done more for me in interviews than any definition.**


My separate note on the "tell me about a project" question, with the structure and a worked example, is on the portfolio [13].

## Coding rounds for GenAI roles

**Expect Python: parse and validate a JSON output against a schema; implement reciprocal rank fusion over two ranked lists; write a retry with backoff around an API call; chunk a text by paragraphs with a size cap; compute cosine similarity; write a small evaluation loop. Rarely leetcode-style puzzles. Write clear, typed, tested code, talk while you write, and handle the edge case out loud. The interviewer is watching how you work, not whether you finish.**


```python
def reciprocal_rank_fusion(*ranked_lists: list[str], k: int = 60) -> list[str]:
    """Fuse ranked lists of ids; 1/(k+rank) per list, summed. A common coding-round question."""
    scores: dict[str, float] = {}
    for ranked in ranked_lists:
        for rank, doc_id in enumerate(ranked, start=1):
            scores[doc_id] = scores.get(doc_id, 0.0) + 1.0 / (k + rank)
    return sorted(scores, key=scores.get, reverse=True)
```

## How should freshers prepare for a GenAI interview?

**Build one RAG project and one fine-tune before the interview, so every answer has a story. Read four papers: transformer, RAG, LoRA, QLoRA. Write the evaluation set for your project, because the evaluation question is where freshers lose. Rehearse the project walkthrough with a timer, failure by failure. Prepare three questions to ask about how the team evaluates and ships. Then be honest about what you have not done; the sentence "I have not done that, here is how I would start" gets hired.**



## Questions to ask the interviewer

**How do you evaluate model changes before they ship? What does your logging show for a bad answer? How often do requirements change and how do you handle it? Who owns prompt versions? What was the last production incident and what changed after? These tell you whether the team treats LLM systems as engineering, and they tell the interviewer you do.**

**I run GenAI interview preparation sessions for final-year batches and tech clubs, with a live system design and a project walkthrough clinic.** Email pranjulrathour41@gmail.com or use pranjulrathour.scult.in/invite.
