# What is YOLO in machine learning? Uses, versions and commercial licensing
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/what-is-yolo-machine-learning/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-23

YOLO, short for You Only Look Once, is a family of deep learning models for real-time object detection: given an image, it predicts boxes around objects and labels them, such as person, car or helmet, in a single pass of the network. That speed made it the default choice for video, robotics and edge devices. This page explains why YOLO is used, how the versions differ, whether it can classify, segment and work on video, the commercial licensing question, how it relates to vision-language models, how it compares with MediaPipe, and how to train one in Colab. What is YOLO in machine learning? YOLO is an object detection model that divides an image into a grid and predicts, in one forward pass, bounding boxes, confidence scores and class labels for objects. It was introduced by Joseph Redmon and colleagues in 2016. Earlier detectors first proposed many candidate regions and then classified each one, which was slow. YOLO framed detection as a single regression problem from image pixels to boxes and classes, trading a little accuracy for a large gain in speed. Later versions improved accuracy with better backbones, multi-scale features, anchor-free heads and training tricks, while keeping real-time performance. The output is a list of boxes with class and confidence, usually cleaned up with non-maximum suppression to remove duplicates. Why is YOLO used? YOLO is used because it is fast, accurate enough for most practical tasks, easy to train on custom data and easy to deploy, from GPUs to phones and edge devices. Also asked as: can yolo be used for commercial use Typical uses: Traffic and vehicle counting from CCTV. Safety compliance, such as helmet and vest detection on construction sites. Retail shelf monitoring and product counting. Crop, pest and fruit detection in agriculture. Robotics and drones that must see in real time. Its ecosystem matters too: tools such as Ultralytics provide training, evaluation and export in a few lines of code, and models export to formats such as ONNX and TensorRT. In FaceVision I ran vision models in the browser with ONNX Runtime Web, and the same export path lets YOLO run client-side. What is the difference between YOLO versions? Versions differ in architecture, accuracy, speed and tooling, and they come from different authors. The original author released v1 to v3; later versions came from other researchers and from Ultralytics, which maintains the most widely used library. A rough map: v1 to v3 (2016 to 2018): the original design, adding anchors and multi-scale prediction. v4 (2020): many training and architecture improvements. v5 and v8: Ultralytics' popular, easy-to-use releases; v8 added an anchor-free head and multiple tasks. v6, v7, v9, v10: research and industry releases with their own trade-offs. YOLO11 and later: newer Ultralytics models with better accuracy per computation. For a new project, start with the latest stable Ultralytics model and compare two sizes on your own data. Can YOLO be used for image classification? Yes. Ultralytics YOLO models include classification variants that predict a single label for a whole image, alongside detection, segmentation and pose models. Use classification when you only need "what is in this image", not where. For example, classifying leaf images as healthy or diseased is a classification task; finding every diseased leaf in a field photo is detection. Classification models are smaller and faster, and need simpler labels: just a folder per class. If you might later need locations or counts, label boxes from the start, because converting a classification dataset into a detection dataset means relabelling everything. For pure classification, other architectures, such as EfficientNet or vision transformers, are also strong options. Can YOLO be used for segmentation? Yes. YOLO segmentation models predict a pixel mask for each detected object as well as its box, which is instance segmentation. Ultralytics provides segmentation versions of its models. Segmentation helps when the shape matters: measuring the area of a crack, counting overlapping fruits, separating people from background, or cutting out products. It needs polygon or mask labels, which take longer to create than boxes, though annotation tools with AI assistance speed this up. Segmentation models are a bit slower than detection models of the same size. If boxes are enough for your decision, use detection; add segmentation only when you need precise outlines. Can YOLO detect objects in video? Yes. YOLO processes each video frame as an image, fast enough for real-time video on a GPU and often on edge devices with smaller models. Tracking links detections across frames so each object keeps an ID. Also asked as: can yolo detect objects from video With Ultralytics, running on a video is one line, and tracking is another: from ultralytics import YOLO model = YOLO(&quot;yolov8n.pt&quot;) model.predict(source=&quot;traffic.mp4&quot;, save=True) # boxes on every frame model.track(source=&quot;traffic.mp4&quot;, save=True) # adds persistent IDs For counting objects crossing a line, use tracking IDs rather than raw detections, or you will count the same car many times. Lower resolution and smaller models increase frame rate. Can YOLO be used commercially? It depends on the model's licence. Ultralytics YOLO models are released under AGPL-3.0, which requires releasing your source code if you distribute or offer the software as a service; closed-source commercial use needs an Ultralytics enterprise licence. Other YOLO implementations have different licences, some more permissive, so check the licence of the exact repository and weights you use, including any pretrained weights and datasets. For college projects, research and open-source work, AGPL is usually fine. For a startup product or client work, decide on licensing before you build, because switching models late means retraining and re-validating. When unsure, ask the licensor or a lawyer; this page is not legal advice. Can YOLO be used with vision-language models? YOLO itself is not a vision-language model; it predicts boxes for a fixed set of classes. But open-vocabulary detectors such as YOLO-World accept text prompts for classes, and YOLO is often combined with vision-language models in pipelines. Also asked as: can yolo used for visual language models Two common patterns: use YOLO to find and crop objects quickly, then ask a vision-language model to describe or reason about each crop; or use a vision-language model to label images automatically, then train a fast YOLO model on those labels for real-time deployment. Open-vocabulary models let you detect "red helmet" or "fire extinguisher" without training a new model, at some cost in speed and accuracy compared with a custom-trained detector. MediaPipe vs YOLOv8: which should I use? Use MediaPipe for ready-made, highly optimised on-device solutions such as face detection, face mesh, hand tracking and pose estimation. Use YOLOv8 or newer when you need to detect your own custom objects or want to train and tune the model yourself. MediaPipe, from Google, provides pipelines that run in real time on phones and in browsers with little setup, and it offers some customisation through model training tools. YOLO gives you more control: custom classes, model sizes, training options and export targets. For a fitness app that counts squats, MediaPipe's pose solution is the quick path. For detecting helmets on a site or pests on leaves, train a YOLO model. Some projects use both. How do I train YOLOv8 in Google Colab? Open a Colab notebook with a GPU, install Ultralytics, upload a labelled dataset in YOLO format with a data.yaml file, train a small model, then evaluate and export it. Also asked as: yolov8 tutorial colab !pip install ultralytics from ultralytics import YOLO model = YOLO(&quot;yolov8n.pt&quot;) # small pretrained model model.train(data=&quot;data.yaml&quot;, epochs=50, imgsz=640) metrics = model.val() # mAP on the validation set model.export(format=&quot;onnx&quot;) # for deployment Label a few hundred images per class with an annotation tool, keep a separate test set, and check predictions visually, not only the mAP number. Save weights to Google Drive, because Colab sessions reset.

# Where do Copilot files go? Uploads, downloads, chat history and limits
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/where-do-copilot-files-go/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-23

Where Copilot files go depends on the account. With a work or school account, files you upload to Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat and documents it creates are usually stored in your OneDrive. With a personal account, files stay attached to the conversation and generated files are offered as a download link. This page explains Copilot versus Copilot Chat, where uploads, downloads and exports end up, what to do when Copilot will not produce a file, whether it reads Excel, how long it keeps history, why it has limits, and how it compares with ChatGPT. Copilot vs Copilot Chat: what is the difference? Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat is the chat assistant included for work and school accounts, grounded in the web and the files you give it. Microsoft 365 Copilot is the paid add-on that also reads your organisation's emails, files and meetings and works inside the Office apps. Also asked as: how does copilot compare to chat gpt The practical difference is reach. Copilot Chat answers from public web content and from documents you upload or open, under enterprise data protection. The full Microsoft 365 Copilot can answer "what did my manager say about the launch?" by searching your mailbox, Teams chats and SharePoint, within your permissions, and it adds features such as meeting recaps in Teams and analysis in Excel. Consumer Copilot, for personal Microsoft accounts, is a third product with its own app and limits. Check the Copilot icon and the account shown in the corner to know which one you are using. Where do Copilot files go? On work and school accounts, files that Copilot Chat receives or creates are generally saved to your OneDrive, in a folder created for Copilot. On personal accounts, they stay with the conversation and you download what you need. The quickest way to find a file is the link in Copilot's reply: open it, then use "open file location" or check the file's path in OneDrive. Documents created inside Word, Excel or PowerPoint with Copilot are ordinary files and save wherever you save them, usually OneDrive or SharePoint. Copilot Pages, the shareable canvas for Copilot responses, are stored in Microsoft's cloud and appear in your Microsoft 365 app. Exact folder names and behaviour have changed over time, so search OneDrive for the file name if the link does not show it. Where does Copilot save files? Copilot saves files where the surrounding app saves them. In Word, Excel and PowerPoint it is your chosen location, usually OneDrive or SharePoint. In Copilot Chat on a work account it is your OneDrive. In consumer Copilot it is your browser's download folder once you download. This matters for two reasons. First, Copilot in Excel and Word works best on files saved to OneDrive or SharePoint, because it relies on the cloud copy; local files can limit features. Second, saved files follow normal sharing rules: a file in your OneDrive is private until you share it, and a file in a team SharePoint site is visible to that team. Rename generated files straight away, because default names such as "Document 3" are hard to find later. Where do files uploaded to Copilot go? On a work or school account, a file you upload to Copilot Chat is generally stored in your OneDrive so Copilot can read it, and it stays covered by your organisation's security and compliance policies. On a personal account, it is kept with that conversation. Uploading a file does not make it public or share it with colleagues. For work accounts, Microsoft states that prompts, responses and uploaded content are not used to train the foundation models and remain inside the Microsoft 365 service boundary. Even so, follow your college or company's data policy: do not upload documents you are not allowed to process with AI tools, such as other people's personal data. If you upload sensitive drafts often, clean up the OneDrive folder now and then. Where do Copilot files export to? Exports go to the app or folder you choose. Copilot responses can be copied, exported to Word or turned into a Copilot Page; downloaded files go to your browser's downloads folder; and Office documents save to OneDrive or SharePoint by default. If you want a response as a document, ask Copilot to create a Word document or use the export option under the response, then open it and save it under a proper name. For tables, ask for an Excel file or copy the table into Excel directly; formatting usually survives the paste. On phones, downloads go to the system's download location or the Files app. If an export link expires, which can happen with generated files, ask Copilot to regenerate the file in the same conversation. Why is Copilot not giving downloadable files? Usually because the product or plan you are using cannot create that file type in chat, the request did not trigger file creation, or the download link expired. Asking explicitly for a named file type often fixes it. Also asked as: why copilot is not giving downloadable files Try these in order: Ask clearly: "Create a Word document named report.docx with this content." Ask for the content as text or a table in the chat, then paste it into Word or Excel yourself. Use Copilot inside the target app instead: Copilot in Word for documents, in Excel for spreadsheets, in PowerPoint for decks. Start a new conversation if the old one is long; long chats behave less reliably. Check whether your organisation has disabled file generation. Copying the content is always the fallback, and it is often faster than fighting the download. Can Copilot read Excel files? Yes. You can upload an Excel file to Copilot Chat and ask questions about it, and Copilot inside Excel analyses the open workbook directly: summaries, formulas, charts, PivotTables and trends. For the best results inside Excel, format the data as a table with Ctrl+T, give each column a clear header, remove merged cells and blank rows, and save the file to OneDrive or SharePoint. Then ask specific questions, such as "which product had the largest month-on-month drop?". In chat, very large workbooks may be summarised rather than read in full, so share a focused sheet. Check any formula Copilot writes on a few rows by hand before trusting the totals. How long does Copilot keep chat history? Consumer Copilot keeps your conversations until you delete them, either one by one or all at once in privacy settings. Work and school accounts keep Copilot interactions according to your organisation's retention policies, which admins set. On work accounts, Copilot interactions are stored within the organisation's Microsoft 365 environment so they can be covered by compliance features such as retention and eDiscovery, the same way email is. Deleting a conversation from your view may not remove the organisation's record if a retention policy applies. On personal accounts you control the history yourself. Either way, assume anything you type may be kept and read later, and keep passwords, keys and personal identity numbers out of every chat. Why does Copilot have a chat limit? Limits keep the service affordable and reliable. Every reply costs computing time, very long conversations exceed what the model can hold in context, and long chats tend to drift and give worse answers. A model can only consider a fixed amount of text at once, its context window. In a long chat, older messages are dropped or summarised, so Copilot can forget instructions you gave at the start. Limits on turns per conversation or requests per day also protect the service at busy times and differ by account type. Work with the limits rather than against them: one conversation per task, a short summary of the important facts when you start a new chat, and the key instructions repeated in your first message. How does Copilot compare to ChatGPT? Both are capable assistants, and Copilot uses OpenAI's GPT models for much of its work. The difference is integration: Copilot is built into Windows, Edge and Microsoft 365, while ChatGPT is a standalone app with its own tools. Choose Copilot if your work happens in Outlook, Word, Excel and Teams, or your organisation provides it with enterprise data protection, because it can see the documents you are working on. Choose ChatGPT if you want one broad assistant with strong voice mode, image generation, custom GPTs and many third-party apps. Many people use both: Copilot for work documents, ChatGPT for learning and side projects. Test both on the same real task before deciding, because model updates change the balance every few months.

# Whisper in Python: install, audio arrays, timestamps, speakers, and self-hosting
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/whisper-ai-python-guide/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-23

Whisper in Python usually means openai-whisper, the open-source package for OpenAI's speech recognition model: install it, load a model and call transcribe on an audio file to get text with timestamps. This page is a developer's guide: setup and Python versions, feeding audio as NumPy arrays, word-level timestamps, adding speaker labels, choosing between self-hosted Whisper and a hosted API, apps built on Whisper, and safety. Speech-to-text is part of my OCR &amp; Speech Workspace, so the advice comes from building with it. What is Whisper in Python? In Python, Whisper is the openai-whisper library, which runs OpenAI's open-source Whisper speech recognition models locally. It transcribes audio in many languages, can translate speech into English, and returns segments with start and end times. It depends on PyTorch for the model and ffmpeg for reading audio files. Model sizes range from tiny to large, trading speed for accuracy. Faster community implementations, such as faster-whisper and whisper.cpp, run the same models more efficiently and are popular in production. The Hugging Face Transformers library also provides Whisper models through its speech recognition pipeline, which is convenient if you already use Transformers. How do I use Whisper AI in Python? Install ffmpeg on your system, install the package, load a model and transcribe. Also asked as: how to use whisper ai in python pip install -U openai-whisper import whisper model = whisper.load_model(&quot;small&quot;) # tiny, base, small, medium, large result = model.transcribe(&quot;lecture.mp3&quot;, language=&quot;en&quot;) print(result[&quot;text&quot;]) for seg in result[&quot;segments&quot;][:3]: print(f'{seg[&quot;start&quot;]:.1f}-{seg[&quot;end&quot;]:.1f}s: {seg[&quot;text&quot;]}') Set the language when you know it, to avoid misdetection on short clips. Use a GPU if available; on CPU, start with small or try faster-whisper. For translation into English, pass task="translate". The result also includes the detected language and segment timings, which you can turn into SRT subtitles with a few lines of code. For very long recordings on limited memory, split the audio into parts of a few minutes, transcribe each, and keep the offsets so every line still points to the right moment in the original file. Does Whisper AI work with Python 3.13? It depends on whether PyTorch and Whisper's other dependencies provide packages for your Python version on your platform. If installation fails on a very new Python, create a virtual environment with a Python version that PyTorch officially supports and install there. Check PyTorch's installation page for the supported Python versions and your operating system and GPU combination, then install the matching PyTorch build before installing Whisper. Most problems on new Python releases come from compiled dependencies not yet published as wheels, which makes pip try to build from source and fail. Using tools such as pyenv or uv to manage several Python versions side by side avoids breaking your system Python. How do I convert any audio file to a NumPy array for Whisper? Whisper expects mono audio sampled at 16 kHz as a float32 NumPy array with values between -1 and 1. Use whisper.load_audio, which calls ffmpeg, or a library such as librosa, then pass the array to transcribe. Also asked as: how to convert any audio file to np.ndarray for openai whisper import whisper, librosa audio = whisper.load_audio(&quot;call.m4a&quot;) # float32, 16 kHz mono via ffmpeg # or: audio, _ = librosa.load(&quot;call.m4a&quot;, sr=16000, mono=True) result = whisper.load_model(&quot;base&quot;).transcribe(audio) If your audio arrives as raw bytes from a microphone or stream, convert integer samples to float32 by dividing by 32768 for 16-bit audio, and resample to 16 kHz. Wrong sample rates produce garbled or sped-up transcripts, a common bug. How do I use whisper_timestamped in Python? whisper_timestamped is an open-source extension of Whisper that adds word-level timestamps and confidence scores. Install it, load a model through it, and call its transcribe function; each segment then includes a list of words with start and end times. Also asked as: how can i properly use whisper_timestamped in python3 import whisper_timestamped as wt audio = wt.load_audio(&quot;talk.mp3&quot;) model = wt.load_model(&quot;small&quot;) out = wt.transcribe(model, audio, language=&quot;en&quot;) for w in out[&quot;segments&quot;][0][&quot;words&quot;][:5]: print(w[&quot;text&quot;], w[&quot;start&quot;], w[&quot;end&quot;], w[&quot;confidence&quot;]) Word timestamps help with subtitles, karaoke-style highlighting and aligning transcripts with slides. Alternatives include WhisperX, which aligns words with a separate model, and the word timestamp option in faster-whisper. Check each project's README for current usage. Does Whisper do speaker diarisation, and how do I add it? No. Whisper transcribes what was said but does not label who said it. To add speakers, run a diarisation model, such as pyannote.audio, to find speaker turns, then assign each transcript segment or word to the speaker active at that time. WhisperX combines these steps. Also asked as: does whisper do speaker diarization? how to add it The pipeline: transcribe with Whisper and get timestamps; run diarisation to get segments like "Speaker 1 from 0.0 to 12.3 seconds"; align by overlapping times; merge consecutive segments from the same speaker. Diarisation works best with clear audio and distinct voices, and struggles with overlapping speech. Some diarisation models require accepting terms and a Hugging Face token. For meetings, many cloud speech services provide diarisation built in. AssemblyAI vs Whisper large-v3: which should you ship? Ship self-hosted Whisper large-v3 when you need privacy, control and low cost at high volume, and can run GPUs. Ship a hosted speech API such as AssemblyAI when you need fast integration, streaming, diarisation and other features out of the box, and accept per-minute pricing and sending audio to a provider. Also asked as: assemblyai vs whisper large-v3: which stt to ship Decide with a test: transcribe 20 to 50 of your real recordings with both, compute word error rate against reference transcripts, and check names, numbers and speaker labels. Also compare latency, uptime commitments, data retention terms and total cost, including your engineering time for GPUs, scaling and monitoring. Accuracy differences vary by accent, domain and audio quality, so public benchmarks are only a starting point. When should I stop self-hosting Whisper? Consider moving to a hosted API when GPU costs and maintenance time exceed API costs, when you need real-time streaming at scale, when reliability requirements outgrow your setup, or when you need features such as diarisation and custom vocabulary without building them. Also asked as: when to stop self-hosting whisper (and what you actually gain Keep self-hosting when privacy or data residency rules require audio to stay on your infrastructure, when volume is high enough that GPUs are cheaper per minute, or when you need full control over models and versions. A useful middle path is a hybrid: self-host batch transcription of sensitive recordings and use an API for live features. Track cost per audio hour and engineer hours monthly to make the decision with numbers. Does Whisper AI have an app? OpenAI does not ship Whisper as a standalone consumer app; Whisper is a model and open-source library. Many third-party apps use Whisper for transcription on desktop and mobile, and OpenAI's own products use speech recognition in features such as voice input. If you want an app, look for transcription apps that state they run Whisper on the device, which keeps audio private, or that use a cloud API, which is faster on weak hardware. Check reviews, privacy policies and whether recordings are uploaded. For developers, a simple personal app is easy to build: a small web page that uploads audio to your own Whisper backend and returns a transcript. Is Whisper AI safe? Whisper itself is safe to use: it is open-source software from OpenAI, and running it locally keeps audio on your machine. Safety concerns come from how you use it and which apps or services wrap it. Points to watch: third-party apps may upload your recordings, so read their privacy policies; Whisper can occasionally produce text that was never spoken, especially during silence or music, which matters for medical, legal or accessibility uses; and recording people requires their consent. Download Whisper and models from official sources, keep dependencies updated, and review transcripts for important decisions.

# Why does Copilot not work? Fixes, offline use, saved chats and credits
URL: https://pranjulrathour.github.io/why-copilot-not-working/
Author: Pranjul Rathour (pranjulrathour41@gmail.com)
Updated: 2026-10-23

Copilot usually stops working because of a sign-in or licence problem, an outdated app, a network or firewall block, a policy set by your organisation, or an outage at Microsoft. It also needs an internet connection, since its models run in the cloud. This page walks through fixes for constant and intermittent failures, what works offline, how long Copilot and Claude keep your chats, and how Copilot credits and Copilot Studio work. Why does Copilot not work? The most common causes are being signed in with the wrong account, a missing licence for the feature you want, an outdated Windows, Edge or Office version, a network that blocks Copilot, or a policy that disables it on work devices. A checklist that fixes most cases: Confirm which account is signed in, personal or work, and that it has the feature. Update Windows, Edge and the Microsoft 365 apps. Sign out completely and sign back in. Try copilot.microsoft.com in a browser to isolate app problems. Switch networks, for example to mobile data, to rule out a firewall or VPN. Ask IT whether Copilot is enabled for your account and device. If nothing works, check Microsoft's service status for an incident. Why does Copilot sometimes not work? Intermittent failures usually come from temporary service load, an expiring sign-in session, unstable network connections, very long conversations, or hitting a usage limit for a feature such as image creation. Patterns and fixes: Fails at busy times: wait a few minutes or retry; heavy load causes timeouts. Fails after a long chat: start a new conversation with a short summary. Fails on one feature only: you may have reached that feature's limit. Fails on campus or office Wi-Fi only: the network may filter some endpoints. Fails after waking the laptop: sign-in tokens may need refreshing; restart the app. Note the time and what you were doing when it fails; patterns point to the cause quickly. Does Copilot work offline? No. Copilot's chat runs on large models in Microsoft's cloud, so it needs an internet connection. Without one, the app cannot send your prompt or receive an answer. Some AI features on Copilot+ PCs run locally on the laptop's neural processing unit, such as certain camera effects, live captions and some image tools, and those can work offline. They are Windows features, not the Copilot chat assistant. If you need an assistant without internet, for example while travelling, you can run a small open-weight model locally with a tool such as Ollama, accepting much lower capability than Copilot or other cloud assistants. Does Copilot work without internet? The Copilot assistant does not work without internet, but you can prepare for offline time: export or copy answers you need, save documents locally, and use on-device Windows features that do not need the cloud. Practical tips for poor connectivity, common on trains and in hostels: draft prompts offline and send them when connected; keep conversations short so they load quickly on slow networks; use the mobile app on mobile data if Wi-Fi is unreliable; and save important outputs as files rather than relying on chat history. GitHub Copilot in your code editor also needs a connection for suggestions, so download documentation you will need for offline coding. Do Copilot chats save? Yes. Consumer Copilot saves your conversations in your account so you can return to them, until you delete them. Work and school accounts store Copilot interactions within the organisation's Microsoft 365 environment. On a personal account, open your conversation history in the Copilot app or website to revisit, rename or delete chats, and use your Microsoft privacy settings to manage stored data. On a work account, your history may be visible to you in Copilot Chat, and the organisation can retain and search interactions for compliance, like email. If you do not want something stored, do not type it into any assistant. GitHub Copilot keeps chat history in your editor session. How long are Copilot chats saved? On personal accounts, chats are kept until you delete them or clear your history. On work and school accounts, the organisation's retention policies decide how long Copilot interactions are kept, which can range from short periods to several years. Deleting a chat on a work account removes it from your view, but a retention policy may keep a copy for compliance. Admins configure these policies in Microsoft Purview, often matching the rules for Teams chats and email. If you need to know your organisation's rules, ask IT or check your company's data policy. For personal accounts, review the privacy dashboard periodically and delete conversations you no longer need. Do Copilot chats expire? Generally no, on personal accounts: conversations stay in your history until you delete them. On work accounts, an organisation's retention policy can delete them automatically after a set time. Some temporary content does expire: generated download links for files can stop working after a while, and very old features or conversation formats can change when Microsoft updates the app. If a chat contains something you will need later, such as code, a plan or an important explanation, copy it into a document or notes app. Chat history is a convenience, not a reliable archive. Does Claude AI save chats? Yes. Claude saves your conversations in your Anthropic account so they sync across the web, desktop and mobile apps, until you delete them. Projects keep their files and instructions as well. You can delete individual chats, and your privacy settings control whether your conversations may be used to improve Anthropic's models; review that setting and choose deliberately. Deleted conversations are removed from your history and deleted from Anthropic's systems after a period described in its privacy policy. Incognito-style chats that are not saved to history are available too. As with any assistant, keep passwords, keys and identity documents out of your chats. How do Copilot credits work? In Copilot Studio, agent usage is measured in Copilot Credits: each interaction or action an agent performs consumes credits from your organisation's capacity, with more complex actions, such as generative answers or autonomous runs, costing more. Consumer Microsoft 365 plans use a separate allowance of AI credits for Copilot in apps. Also asked as: how copilot credits work For organisations, admins buy capacity and assign it to environments, then monitor consumption in the Power Platform admin centre. Agents used by licensed Microsoft 365 Copilot users inside Microsoft 365 may be billed differently from public website agents. Because Microsoft adjusts rates and names, check the current Copilot Studio licensing guide before estimating costs. Designing agents with focused knowledge and fewer unnecessary actions reduces consumption. How does Copilot Studio work? Copilot Studio is a low-code tool where you build an agent from instructions, knowledge sources and actions, test it in a chat pane, then publish it to channels such as Teams, websites and Microsoft 365 Copilot. A language model orchestrates which knowledge and actions to use for each message. The building blocks are knowledge such as websites, SharePoint and uploaded files; actions such as connectors, Power Automate flows and APIs; topics for fixed conversation paths; and triggers for agents that run on events or schedules. Analytics show conversations, success rates and where users get stuck. Agents live in Power Platform environments, so development, testing and production can be separated and governed. Start with one narrow use case and expand after reviewing real conversations.
